name: Red Bull
description:
This is a review of the American version of Red Bull. The first energy drink I ever tried was the original American version of Red Bull.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Itâs not an exaggeration to say that Red Bull is the energy drink that started it all. It can be considered the original taste of energy drinks, and it truly stands as the top energy drink in the world.

The first energy drink I ever tried was Red Bull, and after that, I started trying various energy drinks. But still, Red Bull is always delicious no matter when you drink it! ((o(Â´âï½)o)) The scent is strong, and it immediately gives off that iconic Red Bull smell, making you eager to drink it even before you take a sip.

The sweetness is not overwhelming, and it has a crisp, refreshing taste thatâs easy to drink. The fragrance subtly fills the air with each sip, and even though the taste itself isnât too strong, it combines with the aroma to create a rich flavor.

After trying so many different energy drinks, Iâve come to really appreciate the consistent deliciousness of Red Bull. Honestly, I think I could just stick to drinking Red Bull and not need anything else, because its quality is that high.

There are many misconceptions about the American version of Red Bull, like how itâs stronger than the Japanese version or how the Japanese one is diluted. So letâs clear this up here.

The American version of Red Bull in an 8.4oz (250ml) can contains 80mg of caffeine, the same amount as the Japanese version. The main difference is that it contains taurine, but the amount is only 1,000mg. This is comparable to the amount in drinks like Lipovitan D or other inexpensive energy drinks that cost under 100 yen.

The B vitamins are also nearly the same. In the Japanese version of Red Bull, arginine is used instead of taurine, so itâs not a straightforward comparison. Moreover, since both taurine and arginine are in very small amounts, you wonât feel any significant difference after drinking just one can, and thereâs no clear superiority between these ingredients (just being honest).

Wow! You might think, "The foreign Red Bull is amazing!" but the placebo effect is most likely a factor here. (ï¼Â´âï½)

If you look at the reviews of energy drinks from both abroad and within Japan on Energy Drink Mania, youâll see that the idea of overseas energy drinks being superior is debunked. While there are some intense ones from abroad, those arenât usually found in regular convenience stores or supermarkets, so consider those to be special, unusual energy drinks.

name: Red Bull (Japan)
description:
Red Bull, the global leader with the largest market share, is the original energy drink.

While many people might think it was born in the United States, it was actually created in Austria, Europe. Occasionally, I see articles mistakenly stating that it was born in Australia, but the correct country is Austria.

Red Bull is the ultimate classic, the standard when it comes to the taste of energy drinks. At Energy Drink Mania, weâve come to refer to flavors like Red Bull as "classic flavors," and nowadays, the term "classic flavor" is widely understood.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

With its classic yellow liquid and the intensely fragrant, sweet-tangy aroma... The moment you smell this, you can instantly tell someone is drinking Red Bull, thanks to its distinctive scent.

The flavor is the classic sweet-tangy, bold energy drink taste that everyone knows. It's safe to say this flavor served as the base for the many energy drinks that have developed worldwide.

For those trying Red Bull for the first time, the strong acidity and sweet-tangy, fruity taste may have a somewhat chemical or artificial note. However, after trying various energy drinks, you'll realize there are others with even stronger chemical flavors and aromas, so Red Bull is surprisingly easy to drink.

Although there may be a slight aftertaste, itâs not overwhelmingly sweet, and when chilled, itâs refreshing and quickly quenches your thirst. Drinking Red Bull when you're tired and parched is a special experience (*Â´è¸ï½*)

Since the birth of Red Bull's distinctive taste and aroma, many energy drink brands that rapidly spread across Europe in the 1990s have imitated Red Bull's flavor. Even in the U.S., the world's top market, many brands have created versions inspired by Red Bull's taste, often emphasizing a sweeter, more aromatic flavor or a stronger chemical note.

The "energy drink flavor" most people recognize as Red Bull has created an incredibly vast market, and its 30-plus years of success worldwide is nothing short of miraculous. It's heartening to know that we can enjoy Red Bull so easily here in Japan. The first Red Bull I ever tried was in the U.S. in 2002.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 222mg of arginine. In Japan, arginine is used instead of taurine, which is found in Red Bull sold overseas. Arginine helps with vasodilation and stimulates the secretion of growth hormones. However, with 222mg, you probably won't feel much effect.

The 185ml can Iâm reviewing here was discontinued in 2021. Both the 185ml and 250ml cans contain the same amount of energy ingredients. The 250ml can contains more calories and sugar, so the 185ml can could be considered more concentrated in terms of energy ingredients.

The blue and silver colors are instantly recognizable as Red Bullâs signature look. The logo, featuring two bulls facing each other, is a distinctive feature.

Red Bull, which debuted in Austria in 1987, made its Japanese debut in December 2005. It initially launched as a test product in clubs and bars where Red Bull would be a good fit. Later, on April 4, 2006, 7-Eleven started exclusive early sales in the Kanto and Kansai regions. At first, it was only available at 7-Eleven, making it a sort of limited release.

As weâve covered in past Energy Drink Mania news, the standard products were the 185ml and 250ml cans. Later, the 330ml can was sold exclusively in drugstores, and the 355ml can became available nationwide. A 330ml resealable bottle can was also released.

On June 4, 2013, a limited-edition 330ml PET bottle (300 yen) featuring the band CRACK BANQUET, winners of "Red Bull Live on the Road," was released. However, it was quickly recalled because the expiration date was not listed according to Japanese standards.

In 2021, Red Bull, which had been relatively expensive, was drastically reduced in price. The 185ml can was discontinued, which was inevitable given the times. With more energy drinks like the 500ml size for 200 yen becoming widespread since 2019 and the popularity of the 355ml Monster Energy, it was reasonable for Red Bull to lower its prices as its market share began to be overtaken by Monster Energy.

However, I think it would have been better to keep the 185ml size and offer it for about 150 yen, making it more accessible. Although the 250ml can price was reduced from 241 yen to 190 yen, 200 yen for 250ml still feels high, and the price cut came too late. The balance between size and price was clearly out of sync with competitors, which is unfortunate.

name: Red Bull Sugarfree
description:
This is a review of the American Red Bull Sugar Free. The biggest difference from the Japanese version is that, while itâs sugar-free, itâs not zero-calorie.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The taste is almost the same as Japan's Red Bull Sugar Free, with a moderate sweetness and a strong tartness. The overall Mogu-Mogu texture (smooth and enveloping texture) is well-preserved, giving it a satisfying, sugar-free taste.

Since Red Bull is a European brand, it has the distinctive European trait where "sugar-free means a reduction in sweetness," which is characteristic of the flavor.

You can distinctly taste the artificial sweetener, so if you're sensitive to that particular flavor, this might not be the best choice for you.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine.

name: Red Bull Sugarfree (Japan)
description:
Red Bull Sugarfree. It is available in Japan in 185ml and 250ml sizes, and is notable for being zero calorie and zero sugar. Overseas, it is marketed as "Zero Sugar" for the sugar-free version and "Total Zero" (with slight name variations depending on the country) for the version with zero calories and zero sugar.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

While there are many sweet and rich energy drinks even in sugar-free versions, Red Bull Sugarfree seems to have a stronger grape-like acidity. On the other hand, I wonder if it's okay for a sugar-free drink to still be sweet, so it might be fine to change the flavor to this extent. The sweetness is slightly toned down, and the medicinal taste may have become a bit more pronounced.

When chilled, the sweetness becomes even less noticeable. Drinking an ice-cold Sugarfree will likely make you feel itâs lacking something. The sweetness is greatly reduced, and the characteristic Red Bull aroma lingers. If you want to savor the taste, I recommend drinking it at room temperature.ã½(Â´ã¼ï½)ã

Itâs like the "too beautiful" version of something. While it still retains the Red Bull scent and acidity, the aftertaste is lighter, and the lingering sweetness is gone. If youâre not a fan of regular Red Bull, you might find Sugarfree easier to drink. Itâs still Red Bull-like but with the sweetness dialed back.

On the flip side, those who prefer rich energy drinks may find it too refreshing and feel like itâs a betrayal of the original. Especially those hardcore fans of thick energy drinks who would probably be outraged saying, "Itâs too cold, and it doesn't even taste anymore!"

name: Red Bull Total Zero
description:
This is a review of Red Bull TOTAL ZERO, a zero-calorie, zero-sugar energy drink. Unlike the Sugarfree version, this one has absolutely zero calories.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Red Bull TOTAL ZERO is a fully zero-calorie version. Although Red Bull Sugarfree is labeled zero calories and zero carbs, it actually contains a small amount (10 kcal and 3g carbs per 8.4oz).

The aroma feels slightly weaker than the original Red Bull. The taste is also lighter in terms of both sourness and sweetness compared to the original or Sugarfree versions. With mild carbonation, it has a very smooth mouthfeel and is easy to drink.

Because of the double-zero formula and the slight bitterness from artificial sweeteners, it gives off a somewhat medicinal taste. While this is less noticeable at room temperature, when ice-cold, the flavor becomes harder to detect, which makes the medicinal taste and aroma stand out more.

The aftertaste has almost no sweetness, with a crisp sourness that makes it feel refreshing. Despite the mild carbonation, the clean finish comes from the absence of any lingering residue in the mouth. It's a typical zero-calorie flavor, but the artificial sweetener's bitterness is surprisingly well-masked. However, if zero-calorie drinks arenât your thing, you're better off sticking with the original for a more satisfying experience.

Red Bull â Sugarfree â TOTAL ZEROâthe flavor lightens clearly in that order.

It contains 80mg of caffeine, 1000mg of taurine, and guaranaâjust like the original. Despite having zero sugar and zero calories, the energy ingredients remain the same.

The dark can design might suggest a stronger formula, but in fact, the content is no different from the original version. Donât worryâitâs not stronger just because itâs an international version, so you can enjoy it with peace of mind. (Â´âï½*)

The can is a deep, dark grayâalmost blackâgiving off a strong impression that you wouldn't immediately associate with a zero-zero product.

The pull tab is a dark, nearly black grayâan absolute joy for pull-tab collectors. (âÂ´Ïï½â)

With the original in blue and the Sugarfree in light blue, the only brighter option for clear distinction would have been white or light gray. But Red Bull went the opposite direction with black, which is a bold and refreshing choice.

Most zero-calorie energy drinks tend to use white or silver, so Red Bull choosing black for TOTAL ZERO was quite a surprise at the time.

That said, since the difference between Sugarfree and TOTAL ZERO is so subtle, it does make you wonder if thereâs a strong reason to keep this version on the market. (^_^;)

name: Red Bull Cola
description:
This is a review of Red Bull Cola, which was discontinued in the U.S. due to poor sales. It is also known for being temporarily pulled from shelves shortly after its release due to an issue with its ingredients.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The aroma has a light, Pepsi-like character, while the color is a deep reddish-black with a yellowish brightness, giving it an amber hue somewhere between orange and brown. From this color, it gives the impression that both the aroma and flavor will be mild.

The flavor is a light Pepsi-like taste without any richness. The sweetness is crisp and mild, with no lingering aftertaste. When consumed at room temperature, it is so indistinct that you may struggle to describe itâit's hard to tell if itâs Red Bull Cola or Pepsi.

While it has almost no distinct flavor at room temperature, chilling it thoroughly reveals the flavor Red Bull likely intended. I often taste drinks at room temperature to check their flavor, but itâs been a while since I encountered a flavor that benefits so much from being served cold, lol.

Chilling it balances the sweetness, transforms it into a refreshing sensation, and leaves a pleasant cola aroma, making it more crisp and drinkable than cola or Pepsi.

The aftertaste becomes clean and easy to enjoy, making me think that if there were a large, low-cost version of Red Bull Cola, it could be worth stocking up on as a cola alternative. It offers a unique flavor distinct from Coca-Cola or Pepsi, and the natural ingredients set it apartâthough pricing would be a factor. (Â´ã»Ïã»ï½)

Red Bull Cola is a natural-style energy cola made from natural ingredients. However, it once made headlines when trace amounts of a residual substance from coca leaves, used for flavoring, were detected. Although the amount was so minimal that it posed no risk to human health, it drew significant attention due to its classification as an energy drink (which is often viewed as sweet and unhealthy).

This Red Bull Cola was carefully crafted using only natural ingredients. Although many companies have recently launched natural-oriented products, the attempt to create an all-natural energy cola within the energy drink category still feels impressive today.

The color scheme inevitably resembles Pepsi's branding, making me wonder if they should have gone with a unique edition design to give Red Bull Cola its own distinctive look.

With this uncharacteristic Red Bull design and its natural ingredients, the product presented a fresh image unlike any previous Red Bull offerings. Itâs easy to imagine it being quite a novelty at the time (especially since there was another Red Bull flavor with a more traditional design).

Even after the Edition Series was introduced, Red Bull Cola continued with this design, which is pretty interesting.

The pull-tab was blue. Simply beautiful. (âÂ´Ïï½â)

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2014
description:
This is a review of the Red Bull Summer Edition 2014, which was released as a limited edition tropical fruit flavor in North America starting in the summer of 2014.

After its release in the U.S., it was launched in various European countries and has become a long-running bestseller, continuing to be sold even after more than 10 years. Naturally, it has also become a popular and long-loved flavor in Japan as a regular product.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

News before the Summer Edition release covered this, and it is part of the limited summer Red Bull Edition series. Since it was labeled as a tropical flavor, I imagined it would be sweet and syrupy before trying it.

Upon opening, the scent was surprisingly strong with citrus notes. The flavor was similarly bold with a strong citrus flavor, which was not what I expected. Unlike the sweet tropical fruit flavors, it doesn't leave a heavy aftertaste. Instead, the strong citrus fragrance lingers even after drinking.

The fruits that come through in the Summer Edition are pineapple, guava, passion fruit, lemon, and a hint of mango, creating a satisfying finish with strong acidity and aroma. It's a refreshing and crisp tropical fruit flavor, so even if it's not blazing hot, it's delicious at room temperature. Of course, chilling it makes it even more refreshing, perfect when you want to recharge (*Â´ï½ª`*).

When thinking of tropical flavors, I expected something like Monsterâs M-80, RIPPER, or KNOCKOUT Monky Punch with a rich sweetness, but the Summer Edition turned out to be a much more citrusy and tart fruit flavor.

However, compared to other Edition series flavors, this one aligns with the fresh, tropical vibe it promises.

Since Red Bull is juice-free, I guess making it overly rich would risk ruining the image with added thickeners or the like.

In the 355ml can, it contains 114mg of caffeine. This is the same amount as the other Red Bull drinks (32mg/100ml). The other ingredients are almost identical to the usual Red Bull.

While the North American version is 355ml, in some parts of Europe, it is actually sold in 250ml cans, so the ingredient amounts may vary in those cases. Either way, the caffeine content and sugar levels arenât too high, making it an accessible limited-edition Red Bull for many.

But the silver pull tab is a letdown... (ã½Â´Ï`)

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2015 (Japan)
description:
Finally, the Red Bull Summer Edition with a tropical fruit flavor has been released for the summer of 2015 in Japan! Unlike in the U.S. and other countries, this version has a unique, original flavor that includes a hint of yuzu, making it exclusive to Japan.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

First, I participated in the Tropicaru Party held at the Red Bull headquarters the day before the release of Red Bull Summer Edition, where I was given a can by a Red Bull Girl. I drank it there and then re-tasted it the following morning to give a comprehensive review. (I had already drunk 6 cans the previous day! (^_^;))

When I opened the can, a refreshing citrus-like orange scent spread. It wasnât overpowering, but it had a fresh scent, unlike the strong tropical fruit aroma.

The color is yellow, just like the overseas version, with a bright tropical yellow, distinct from the original Red Bull color.

When I tried the Japanese-exclusive Summer Edition, I was surprised to find it... ( ï¾Ð´ï¾)ï¾ï½¯! Itâs weak!! Compared to the Summer Edition I had in America, the taste is quite different. To put it simply, it tastes much milder overall. Although the American Summer Edition isnât particularly intense, it has a punchy citrusy tropical fruit flavor, so this difference is noticeable.

The fruits used are primarily mandarin oranges, mixed with tropical fruits like papaya and passion fruit. Itâs a much lighter citrus-based flavor, reflecting a more Japanese taste profile. While it doesnât have a sharp intensity, the mild acidity makes it easy to drink. Itâs quite refreshing, and I could drink it every morning during the summer (âÂ´Ïï½â).

At the Tropicaru Party the day before, I overheard some insider information: âThe Japanese Summer Edition was designed to recreate the flavor of mandarin oranges and yuzu.â This was something only people who attended the party could hear (*Â´ï½ª`*).

Indeed, the dominant flavor is not a tropical orange but the distinctive mandarin orange taste, and when I heard about yuzu, I could definitely understand how the refreshing flavor could resemble yuzu. Itâs quite different from the rich, tropical pineapples and mangoes.

The Japanese flavor is distinctly created with âmandarin oranges and yuzu.â Itâs a tropical fruit mix that doesnât lean too much into the South Pacific fruits, but rather uses fruits from Japan, making it a unique take.

Some people might be disappointed that the flavor is altered for the Japanese market, but I think it was a good choice to make it more accessible and familiar to Japanese consumers, using mandarin oranges and yuzu.

Like other Red Bull drinks, the Summer Edition contains 80mg of caffeine, 300mg of arginine, and more.

I definitely drank too much at the party the day before, and I can confirm that this tropical fruit flavor works really well as a cocktail base, so be careful when mixing it with alcohol (^_^;).

If you're at a party or enjoy alcohol, particularly with energy drink cocktails, itâs easy to go overboard. â Risks and Precautions About Energy Drink Cocktails

On the other hand, this flavor blends well in cocktails, which shows how delicious it is. Even though Red Bull doesnât have an extremely high caffeine content, five cans will still exceed 300mg, so you need to be careful.

The top of the can features blue stripes. While the Blue Edition had silver stripes, the Summer Edition has a bright, shiny blue. I really like this design (ï½_ï½*). The phrase âTropical Energy Chargeâ feels a bit too typical of Japanese energy drinks, thoughâ¦!

The combination of yellow and blue is common in other Summer Editions, and even Swedenâs version has a similar blue theme. Itâs nice that Japan also adds its own unique color to the mix.

By the way, the pull tab is silver, which is consistent with the American and other international versions.

As the energy drink market continues to grow during the summer, I hope more people get to enjoy the deliciousness of Red Bull Summer Edition and the fun of energy drinks! ((o(Â´âï½)o))

name: Red Bull Spring Edition 2016: Sakura (Japan)
description:
The world's first flavor, released exclusively in Japan and for a limited time, the pink Red Bull Spring Edition. The flavor is Sakura, so I was curious about what it would taste like. Thanks to the Red Bull Friends initiative, I was able to get it before its official release, so letâs dive into the review! ((o(Â´âï½)o))

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When you open the can, a sweet and sour, slightly artificial scent wafts out. The actual scent of cherry blossoms isnât that strong, so thereâs no immediate association of "this scent must be cherry blossoms." It left me wondering, "What exactly does the Sakura flavor smell like?"

Unlike the strong fruity scents of the Summer Edition or Grape Edition , this one has a subtle, sweet and sour floral fragrance.

When you pour it into a glass, itâs a bright, clear, calming pink just as expected (Â´âï½*). Itâs a lighter pink than Rockstar's Perfect Berry, and has a warm, cheerful pink typical of Sakura in Japan. Make sure to hold the glass and admire it from different angles. You'll feel its beauty, which is different from the intense pinks often seen in energy drinks (âÂ´Ïï½â).

As for the taste... itâs a unique blend of acidity and smooth sweetness that harmonize without any awkwardness. Itâs neither a fruit flavor nor a chemical, overly artificial taste... Itâs a Sakura flavor that leaves you wondering, "What does Sakura taste like?"

If you try to categorize the flavor, itâs something like Acerola, ume (plum), or slightly sour cherries (mild cherries). It's certainly not a definitive âSpring Edition flavorâ in terms of taste.

I wondered where this confusion about the taste came from... and I realized it might be because of the distinct, lightly floral fragrance associated with Sakura. This aroma makes it difficult to form a clear taste image, resulting in an indescribable flavor. Try drinking it without breathing through your nose and avoiding the fragrance.

Youâll notice a more pronounced taste of smooth acidity and flavors reminiscent of Acerola or sweet ume. The floral fragrance alone changes how you perceive the flavor (ï¾ï¼¡ï¾;)ï½ºï¾ï½¸ï¾.

I think many people who tried it before its official release might have felt "I donât really get the taste." Itâs hard to imagine how many people would think, "Itâs so good, I want to buy it again!"

Basically the same as the original Red Bull. It contains 80mg of caffeine, 222mg of arginine, and other similar energy drink ingredients.

Red Bull is known for being fruit juice-free and creating flavors from other ingredients, but I think it would be interesting if they started incorporating unique ingredients specific to each flavor. The Sakura flavor in the Spring Edition could really benefit from this approach! ((o(Â´âï½)o)).

I didnât expect the pink to have such an impact when I first held the can. Thereâs no unnecessary decoration, and the subtle pink is both very Japanese and very Red Bull-like. It was funny seeing my Twitter feed turn pink.

Some pictures online have edited the color to a harsh pink, but the actual can color is a very soft pink (âÂ´Ïï½â).

The Sakura motif used in the flavor name display, which has been adopted globally since 2015, perfectly expresses the Sakura flavor, showcasing the uniqueness of this edition. Itâs also a world-first experiment.

Another notable detail is the faint pink print of the bull on the ingredients list. Previously, such colorful prints were rare.

Personally, I think if the can were the globally standard 250ml size, its beauty would be even more pronounced. The 185ml can is adorable, but I think a 250ml version would give it a more mature vibe.

The pull tab is of course silver, which is to be expected... But since the Edition series is expanding globally, I look forward to seeing tabs in different colors in the future.

Given all the design constraints, Iâm happy to see such a spring-like, distinctly Japanese Sakura design on the can. The Sakura flavor might spark some debate, but I believe they captured the essence of what Japanese people would expect from a Spring Edition.

Also, I hope Red Bull continues the pre-release gift campaign with the two-can set delivered in this box. This yearâs Sakura design is my favorite one yet (ï½_ï½*).

name: Red Bull Orange Edition
description:
The ORANGE EDITION was released in the United States in February 2016. Unlike the Zero-Zero ORANGE EDITION released in 2015, this one features a new normal tangerine flavor.

The total edition version has already disappeared, so this ORANGE EDITION will remain as the standard color edition product moving forward. â On February 1, 2022, a unique flavor version was released in Japan as a limited edition with a new specification!

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opening the can, the aroma doesnât burst out strongly, and itâs rather mild compared to the bright color of the can. When poured into a glass, a subtle sweetness reminiscent of sugary syrup fills the air, but it doesnât smell like orange.

The color of the drink is a bright orange, more transparent than I expected, resembling caramel in color, rather than the dense orange I had imagined, similar to Monster Chaos.

Upon tasting, the cotton candy-like sweetness and lingering acidity overwhelm the taste of orange and tangerine, and for a moment, itâs hard to tell if itâs an orange-flavored drink at all. Itâs a bit of a disappointment if you were expecting the rich, strong orange flavor of Chaos.

From the vibrant orange can, I had hoped for a more fruity flavor, but instead, it lacks the fruitiness I imagined, and the aftertaste is not pleasant. Itâs the most artificial flavor among the Edition series.

While drinking, I thought it could pass as an orange sports drink without any issues. Itâs a shame itâs not a flavor you savor like the Red Edition or Blue Edition.

With 114mg of caffeine, 1000mg of taurine, and similar ingredients to regular Red Bull, it left me wondering if artificial sweeteners were used, but I found that they werenât.

Like most Edition series drinks, this one is made without fruit juice, but I wish it had a bit more of a juice-like essence, especially with the tangerine flavor. I feel like they reached the limits of flavor reproduction here.

The can design is bold with a bright orange color, which I personally liked a lot, but the taste didnât quite match the image I had from the can, making it a bit disappointing. I think a punchier orange flavor wouldâve been better.

If Iâm choosing orange, I would likely go for the more affordable Juice Monster Chaos .

The pull tab is silver. When the Yellow Edition was revamped around the same time, it got a yellow tab, so if the Orange Edition continues, Iâm hoping for an orange tab.

I purchased it while traveling around East Los Angeles. On that scorching hot February day, I wonder if it would have tasted different had I chugged it down at that time, but the artificial aftertaste probably wouldnât have been refreshing enough to quench my thirst.

â On February 1, 2022, a unique flavor version was released in Japan as a limited edition with a new specification!

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2016 Kiwi Twist
description:
This is the 2016 Summer Edition released in May 2016 in the U.S., featuring a kiwi flavor called Kiwi Twist. It was also released in Europe in 2016.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening the can, a sweet and sour fragrance immediately burst out. However, what is that scent? It doesnât really smell like kiwi, and itâs hard to describe. Itâs similar to the feeling in Japan's Spring Edition , where the scent doesn't exactly evoke kiwi.

When poured into a glass, the liquid is transparent with a pale lime green color. I had imagined a more vibrant and rich green, so this color and fragrance made me think the taste would be quite light.

Upon tasting it... the flavor was completely different from what I imagined. The sweetness of the kiwi is faint, and a strong sourness combined with the sweeteners gives a hint of kiwi-like flavor, but the sourness lingers and creates an artificial taste, which was disappointing.

In my wild imagination, I expected a more intense and juicy kiwi fruit sweetness, followed by a stimulating sourness, leaving a refreshing, bubbly aftertaste... a more full-bodied, fruity kiwi flavor. But instead, it turned out to be the oppositeâan artificial and hard-to-grasp taste. I suppose it's unrealistic to expect so much from a drink with no actual fruit juice in it (laughs). This is a sign of how high the expectations are for the Edition series.

Compared to the Orange Edition released in 2016, this has lost the vibrant fruitiness that made past Editions so impressive, now tasting quite artificial... (ã½Â´Ï`)

The energy ingredients are the standard Red Bull formula, with 114mg of caffeine and taurine, but not much else to note.

People who say Red Bull is dangerous should take a look at the ingredient list. Everything that is included and not included is clearly stated.

I like this color, but since the taste was different from what I imagined, Iâm left wondering if the can design is the only good thing about it (laughs).

The back features the 2016 design, where the blue now has color. The Yellow Edition, which had a yellow tab in 2016, was all silver. In Japan, the 2016 Summer Edition is silver and yellow, and the Spring Edition is silver and pink. This seems to be the trend for this year.

The pull tab is unfortunately silver. I wonder if theyâll change to a colored tab like the Yellow Edition sometime in the future?!

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2016: Zwetschke-Zimtnelke
description:
This is a review of the RED BULL WINTER EDITION 2016 Zwetschke-Zimtnelke, the first-ever winter-themed Red Bull, which was released exclusively in Austria in preparation for the winter of 2016.

I had a feeling that a winter edition would eventually be released in some country, but I never expected it to be launched in Austria, the home country of Red Bull...

*Note: In 2017, the same winter edition was released outside of Austria, but it became a fruit flavor without the cinnamon.*

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, a berry-like aroma is released with a hint of spiciness. The flavor is prune and cinnamon.

The color in the glass is surprisingly elegant, with a calm and radiant purple. Itâs not too blue, but has a faint reddish tint, making it look almost magical (*Â´è¸ï½*). It also gives off a prune-like vibe.

When you bring it to your nose, the concentrated aroma of raisins is quite strong. Unlike the fresh berry-like scent I first noticed, the rich aroma makes you think, "Yes, this is definitely prune." Let's try drinking it now!

The first impression of the taste is that itâs a tangy raisin or prune, with very little sweetness. The fruitâs tartness and freshness persist, giving a deep and complex flavor. This can be said to be a high-level edition, a rare one weâve been waiting for. It's on the same level or even better than the original Red Bull or Blue editions. Iâve been waiting for something like this! (*Â´ï¼Ïï¼`*)

The more you drink, the more you are "brainwashed" by the prune flavor, with its tartness and astringency. Furthermore, a subtle cinnamon flavor starts to appear halfway through, leaving a pleasant aftertaste. Itâs not heavy, but still a rather intense flavor.

This calm flavor makes it perfect for sipping slowly by the fireplace on a cold winter night. If served ice-cold, it would be a shame as the flavor would be lost (^_^;)

Later, I tried chilling it, but I could hardly taste the cinnamon flavor. This is truly a flavor that should be enjoyed at room temperature during winter. Without the cinnamon aroma, you might dismiss it as "just another sour and astringent blueberry flavor." Red Bull really nailed it here (âÂ´Ïï½â).

Now, letâs not worry about savoring it and just gulp it down! When you take large sips, you can feel the heavier, astringent prune taste even more intensely. Since you drink it quickly, the cinnamon flavor comes a bit later, lingering in the throat and escaping through the nose. No matter how you drink it, itâs delicious Î£(Â´âï½ï¼).

Personally, I really enjoy complex flavors like this one from the Winter Edition. It's like wine or beerâit's fun to think about the layers of taste.

Since the 2015 Orange Edition, the series had started to feel like it had cheapened, but this edition brings a shock with its next-level taste. It surpasses the level of soda, standing in a league of its own. Before drinking, I thought maybe cinnamon didnât need to be added, but I was wrongâthis is exactly how it should be (*Â´ï½ª`*).

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine. As usual, the ingredient composition is nothing out of the ordinary. Thereâs no extra punch like the overseas versions.

First of all, the color of the can is wonderful. It has warmth and a sense of luxury. The balance of colors between the can and the contents is well thought out and stylish.

The ingredient list is positioned so it doesnât obscure the bull logo.

I suddenly realized that the subdued main color and design seem to match the calm color of the flavor name itself. Other editions tend to use silver or colors that match the canâs theme, but the Winter Edition uses gold, which makes it stand out from previous editions.

Itâs not flat but instead has a sophisticated and warm charmâvery stylish (âÂ´Ïï½â). If the flavor name was in silver, the overall impression would have been much weaker.

The tab is silver, as itâs the Austrian version. If the tab were the same color as the can, Iâd probably freak out!

The worldâs first Winter Edition was released in Austria in 2016. The snowflake imagery is the best representation of the experience for those who have tried it.

The following year, in 2017, it was also released in South Korea and Germany, but countries like Canada and the U.S. got a version without cinnamon, called "Plum Twist."

Since the taste is completely different, you wonât be able to enjoy the rich flavor and aroma of this edition in North America. Due to the flavor difference, itâs almost like a completely different product, which is a shame. Unfortunately, you wonât get to enjoy the plum-cinnamon combination thatâs perfect for a slow, cozy winter night.

Iâm not sure why they decided to remove the cinnamon and the rich, calming plum combination. Luckily, when I traveled to South Korea, I managed to find some expired stock of the Winter Edition, and I was able to enjoy the same flavor as Zwetschke-Zimtnelke. For global products, it would be great if they could keep the flavor consistent across all regions.

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2017 Plum Twist
description:
In 2017, the Plum Twist flavor of Red Bull Winter Edition was released in several countries, including Canada.

This is different from the Plum Cinnamon flavor that was first released as the Winter Edition in Austria in 2016, which can be found at this link . The Plum Twist offers a simple fruit flavor with just plum.

By 2018, it was launched in the United States and other countries, making it one of the season edition flavors with the most staggered release dates worldwide.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, a sweet and sour aroma of plum, cherry, and berry spreads. Unlike the 2016 Winter Edition, there is of course no cinnamon scent. Let's try it as a completely different flavor. When you take a sip, you are enveloped in a rich taste and aroma of sweet and sour plum, cherry, and blackberry. If the acidity were too strong, the flavor could become light, but Plum Twist maintains a strong plum flavor throughout due to the presence of sugar and the intensity of its aroma. This is delicious~ (*Â´è¸ï½*)

Although there is no real fruitiness, the balance between the intensity of the sweet and sour flavor and the strong aroma is excellent, and the lingering plum aroma ensures that this flavor is definitely satisfying to drink.

There is almost no aftertaste left in the mouth after drinking. The acidity doesn't linger on the tongue for long, and despite the strong flavor, it is easy to drink and enjoyable.

If you've ever tried the 2016 Winter Edition Zwetschke-Zimtnelke (Plum Cinnamon flavor) , you might compare it, but if you evaluate Plum Twist purely on its own, I think it's more than good enough for the Edition series, and I highly recommend it to those who seek a strong energy drink flavor.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine. There are no special energy ingredients, and it has the same composition as regular Red Bull. As with other Edition series, it has no fruit juice. However, the sweet and sour taste and rich aroma still offer a fruit-like experience.

I compared the Canadian Plum Twist, released in 2017, with the American version, which was released a year later in 2018.

The color remains unchanged, and of course, the aroma is exactly the same.

Since there was a one-year gap in release dates, I thought there might be a difference in taste, but the taste and aroma are exactly the same. Both offer the sweet and sour, rich plum and berry flavors.

It's great that the North American Red Bull Edition series comes in the 355ml big size, allowing you to enjoy more of it. Plus, it remains delicious and enjoyable until the very end.

Now, the main topic begins here. Unlike the North American Winter Edition, which has a plum flavor, the German and Korean versions retain the spicy Plum Cinnamon flavor from the original Austrian version. I already know the taste difference, but Iâd like to compare them just to show the differences.

First, let's compare with Germany. On the left is the Canadian version (355ml), and on the right is the German version (250ml). The color is almost the same, but the aroma is completely different. The German version has a more subdued fruity aroma with a slight hint of cinnamon spice.

The base flavor of the German version is still plum, but with a milder acidity, the plum flavor feels much more subdued. There is a slight acidity, but the cinnamon aroma drifts through and provides a calming feeling. Adding cinnamon makes a big difference.

If you enjoy "fruity and sweet-sour rich flavors," you might find the North American Plum Twist more delicious.

Next, I opened the Korean version. When you open the Korean Winter Edition, the cinnamon aroma is quite strong. On the left is the Canadian version (355ml), and on the right is the Korean version (250ml).

The color of the Korean version is more reddish, unlike the bluish-purple hue of the North American version. It's a bit hard to tell...

This difference comes from the fact that Korean Red Bull is slightly unique. I thought there would be a larger difference compared to the German version, but the color difference is even more noticeable.

The Korean Winter Edition has a stronger cinnamon spice aroma, and the plum flavor itself feels a little heavier than the Canadian version. When chilled, the taste and aroma tend to fade, so itâs best enjoyed at a temperature closer to room temperature to savor the full flavor and aroma. After drinking, the cinnamon aroma lingers pleasantly, giving a cozy winter feel, which is perfect for a winter version of Red Bull.

Given it's a winter edition, I personally think a warm, cinnamon-flavored drink suits the season better.

The Plum Twist can be enjoyed all year round, even outside the winter season.

Seasonal editions often turn into regular products the following year, and it might have been more convenient to have the simple plum edition available year-round.

The tab is a silver tab. If it becomes a regular product, it might even be available with a colored tab, like yellow, green, or orange (which all had colored tabs).

The Red Bull Winter Edition Plum Twist that was released in Canada in 2017. I thought it might be rebranded as the "Plum Edition" and become a regular product the following year, but in 2018, it wasnât made a regular product.

However, for some reason, the same Winter Edition Plum Twist from 2017 returned as a limited edition in Canada in 2018. This is the first time a season edition has been released two years in a row. Perhaps it was so popular in Canada that they decided to bring it back!

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2017 Grapefruit Twist
description:
This is a review of the 2017 limited edition Summer Edition, RED BULL SUMMER EDITION 2017 Grapefruit Twist. It's truly a summer-like flavor, perfectly fitting for a Summer Edition with a taste that suits the season.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a strong, bitter grapefruit aroma bursts out. Wow... this is really promising ((o(Â´âï½)o)) The color is rich and red, making you want to drink it right away! When poured into a glass, the scent changes, and in addition to the bitter grapefruit aroma, there's also a sweet, syrupy scent floating in the air. Huh? This is a bit off, isn't it?

Taking a sip... it has a slightly bitter grapefruit flavor with restrained sweetness, leaving no aftertaste. The rich citrus scent doesn't linger much after drinking, instead leaving a refreshing and smooth sensation. Wow, it's delicious... The sweet scent was a bit concerning, but once I tasted it, the intense, bitter fruit flavor overwhelmed me.

The bitterness of the grapefruit lingers pleasantly, and thanks to the sugar, there's no thinness, with a perfect balance of bitterness and acidity. It's easy to drink, and the fruity sensation is nicely presented. Overall, it has no unpleasant aftertaste and is a pink grapefruit flavor that anyone can enjoy. I'll definitely drink this up quickly...

If this were made with fruit juice, it would probably have a lingering, overpowering aftertaste. That would have its own deliciousness, and I'd probably become hooked, but the non-juice grapefruit twist offers a refreshing and balanced taste that you can't get with fruit juice, which is what's so great about it. I think the recipe for this one is a success.

You can enjoy the fruitiness while also experiencing a refreshing taste that's impossible to achieve with fruit juice. It's so delicious that the 355ml can feels more like a 250ml one, and I've ended up drinking it all in one go, which is a bit of a problem (^_^;)

Since the latter half of 2016, I feel like the development team must have changed, because the deliciousness of the editions made a remarkable comeback with this one.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1250mg of taurine, among other ingredients. This is one of the most drinkable Summer Editions, so personally, I think I need to be cautious about over-consuming caffeine.

It reminds me of the 2014 Tropical Edition, where I could easily drink multiple cans. If I used this in cocktails, I'd definitely end up drinking too much (^_^;)

For the 2017 Summer Edition, the flavor name is in gold, just like the 2016 Winter Edition. The can design itself is similar, and depending on the lighting, you might mistake it for the Winter Edition at first glance.

When you line them up, the difference becomes clear. The Grapefruit Twist can has a more flat red design, which lacks the premium feel and looks more like the usual line. It gives off a slightly matte impression.

Here, Iâve lined up the Summer Edition with the Red Edition and Winter Edition. You can see the difference with the Summer Edition being matte, and there are subtle differences in color when lined up.

It would be great if more flavors were added in the future, allowing for a gradient effect with colors other than red (âÂ´Ïï½â)

The Grapefruit Twist has already been confirmed to become a regular edition, so countries where this is available all year round must be envious. In Japan, seasonal limited editions have already stopped, but I hope they continue to release limited flavors once a year, even if just for the Summer Edition.

This is the 2nd best flavor they ever made! Please bring it back!!!

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2018 Coconut Berry
description:
This is a review of the Red Bull SUMMER EDITION 2018 Coconut Berry.

In the United States, the Summer Edition is released every year in the first week of May, so it has become a tradition for me to travel to the U.S. during Golden Week, the perfect travel season, and buy it (âÂ´Ïï½â).

Although Iâm not particularly fond of coconut scent, and wouldnât say I really love it, I wondered if Iâd be able to finish the entire 355ml... But there was no need to worry. Now, I can happily enjoy chilled Coconut Berry flavors from different countries.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. Upon opening, a strong sweet coconut scent wafts through, along with a hint of apple. While itâs labeled as a "Coconut Berry" flavor, the berry scent might not be as prominent from the aroma.

Look at this color! A vibrant summer-like light blue. No matter how many times I drink it, this refreshing and vivid color feels just right for an energy drink and gives off a summer vibe. Itâs wonderful (*Â´ï½ª`*)

As soon as I take a sip, the distinct coconut scent fills my senses, accompanied by a smooth sweetness and a green apple tartnessâ¦ but where is the berry flavorâ¦!?

After getting used to it, the coconut scent no longer bothers me, and the smooth and refreshingly tart green apple flavor stands out. Drinking this makes you wonder, âWhat exactly does a berry flavor taste like again?â (laughs)

By the way, the delicious apple flavor is very similar to the taste of Boston Americaâs Sonic Energy Drink . The lack of berry taste might be because there isnât much tartness or the sweetness is more mellow.

The aftertaste leaves a gentle tartness, and the coconut scent lingers just faintly. Itâs a well-balanced, crisp taste with little aftertaste. When chilled, the tartness stands out more, making it easy to drink. Itâs genuinely delicious (*Â´è¸ï½*)

If you're not bothered by coconut water, youâll likely enjoy the aroma without any issue. Personally, I donât love the sweet scent of coconut, but I find it fine at this level.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine. Of course, thereâs no fruit juice. However, itâs impressive how the coconut aroma and the refreshing, fruity tasteâdespite not being very berry-likeâare achieved. Truly remarkable.

The simple white can with blue "Coconut Berry" lettering looks cool. When displayed in stores in the U.S., the white can of Coconut Berry stood out quite a bit among the colorful edition series. It has a cool and clean image, and personally, I love this color.

However, with the coconut white design, it feels like weâve almost run out of can color options. It might be interesting if they release cans with patterns in the future ((o(Â´âï½)o))

There are already plenty of limited edition cans like that, and it would be great to see it released as a special limited flavor like Red Bull EDIÄION LIMÃN . The design of that one is fantastic.

Since itâs a new release, it comes with the usual silver tab. Recently, many of the existing edition series have been switching from silver to colored tabs, so if this becomes a regular after the season ends, we might see a white tab for Coconut Berry.

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2018 Rumtopf
description:
Released in Austria in 2018, the Red Bull WINTER EDITION Rumtopf.

In 2019, a very similar Winter Edition was released in countries outside of Austria, but the flavor is slightly different in the original Austria release. It really feels like the flagship product from Austria has a stronger sense of craftsmanship... and itâs truly wonderful.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The contents are orange, just like the color of the can. It might look like orange juice, but the scent is completely different, with a rich and tangy fragrance that reminds me of apple pie or cherry pie. Traditional "Rumtopf," which is made by soaking seasonal fruits, often turns a dark red color after being soaked for a long time. However, Red Bull's version of Rumtopf is slightly cloudy orange, which feels a bit strange.

The sweet and heavy aroma spreads with a fruity, tangy taste. The flavor of apple, raisin, and berry, which have been slowly soaked in sugar, stands out with a sweet and sour taste. Surprisingly, it's not as strong as the scent, and it's quite refreshing to drink.

The sweet fragrance and flavor have the taste of syrup soaked in sugar, with the rich flavor of softened fruits as if you're eating fruit soaked in syrup. I can't help but think that if this had real fruit juice, it would have been even more amazing, but I'm impressed with how Red Bull Austria managed to recreate this flavor without any juice.

According to locals, Rumtopf is a traditional winter alcoholic drink made by soaking fruits, sugar, and rum in a rum pot.

People tend to add their favorite fruits, such as strawberries, apples, apricots, red berries, blueberries, and raisins. You can see how it's made in a simple video from someone who is soaking fruits.

They usually let it sit in a cool, dark place for a few months to half a year, and then enjoy it during Christmas or New Year's. It's great that anyone can easily make it.

Here's a video of someone opening Rumtopf made in the summer at Christmas.

This looks delicious... I imagine buying a bunch of berry fruits at the farmer's market and making my own Rumtopf... just the thought of it is exciting. I think I'll make it myself at home (*Â´ï½ª`*)

In other videos, the Rumtopf looks red and cloudy, and I wish Red Bull's WINTER EDITION 2018 had been that red, cloudy color too.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine. The same ingredients as other Red Bull products.

Since Rumtopf is an alcoholic drink made with rum, Red Bull is, of course, non-alcoholic.

You can see the asterisk next to the flavor name on the can. If you look at the back, it says "Alkoholfrei," which means alcohol-free. When an alcoholic beverage name is used in the flavor name, it is usually stated as "non-alcoholic" on the back. Other examples of this include Bang's champagne.

The Red Bull WINTER EDITION Rumtopf was released in Austria in 2018. The following year, similar winter editions were released worldwide, but the flavors are different from Rumtopf. So, let's compare the taste from three countries. From left to right: Austria 2018, Germany 2019, and Canada 2019.

The contents are almost the same orange color. Only the original Austrian version is slightly cloudy. You wouldn't really notice the difference unless you line them up.

The flavor names are Rumtopf, Spiced Cherry (Spekulatius-Kirsch), and Holiday Spice. Since only Rumtopf is named after an alcoholic drink, it's understandable that this one is the only one with cloudiness.

The fragrance is almost identical across all three countries. But are there any taste differences? Let's try them.

The Austrian Rumtopf has a mellow, sweet and sour flavor, while the German and Canadian versions have a more noticeable tartness, with flavors of cherry and berry. There is a hint of cinnamon-like spice in the aroma, but it doesn't affect the taste.

They all offer a rich flavor, and while the flavors are close, you can clearly see that the Austrian version has a more distinctive fruity richness from the soaked fruits.

Whether you prefer the constantly rich taste of Rumtopf or the more refreshing fruitiness of the 2019 worldwide Winter Edition is up to personal taste.

Personally, Iâm happy I got to learn about Rumtopf through the Winter Edition and could taste it, albeit in a simulated form. It was definitely worth hunting it down in Austria . Iâm thinking of making my own Rumtopf starting this summer (*Â´ï½ª`*)

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2019 Holiday Spice
description:
Released in 2019, the Winter Edition Holiday Spice was a winter limited edition product.

Originally, it was a global version of the Winter Edition that was first released in Austria in 2018. The taste is different from the original Austrian version, so I will review them separately.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Despite being a cherry-flavored drink, the can is orange, and so is the contents. The original Austrian Winter Edition Rumtopf and this Canadian Holiday Spice both have flavors and colors that seem somewhat mismatched, creating a slight sense of inconsistency.

When you take a sip, the cherry flavor is refreshing and mild. It's not a rich, sweet, or sour cherry taste. You don't really get a strong sense of the sweetness, tartness, fruitiness, or fragrance of cherry, as everything is balanced and smooth, so you might not feel satisfied with just a 250ml can.

In Canada, alongside the 250ml, a 355ml size is also released, which is a much better quantity. Before you know it, the 355ml is gone... (^_^;)

The flavor is described as cherry and spice, and it differs from the original Austrian Winter Edition. As for the spiced flavor in the Holiday Spice, it's quite subtle... You could say thereâs a hint of cinnamon, but unless you're paying attention, you might not even notice it.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine. As with other Red Bull products, it doesnât contain any fruit juice. Since Canada has two official languages, English and French, the packaging is labeled in both languages.

In Canada, limited edition releases happen every year, and both the 250ml and 355ml sizes are released at the same time. With a cherry flavor and an orange can, it still feels a bit off. The contents are also orange, which makes you think it's an orange-flavored drink (^_^;) I think the issue started with the original Austrian release using this color. If it had been a slightly more subdued orange, it might have looked more fitting for the winter season.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2019 Beach Breeze
description:
Released in late April 2019, the Red Bull Summer Edition Beach Breeze from the U.S. This is one of the most unique flavors in the Red Bull Seasonal Edition seriesânot necessarily bad, but a drink that will likely divide opinions dramatically.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Opening the can releases a somewhat coconut-like scent, along with a sweet, hard-to-describe fragrance that I can't quite place. In fact, the 2018 Summer Edition had a coconut flavor. It's now sold regularly as the Coconut Edition, so it doesn't feel as special, and there's a strong impression of "Another coconut flavor this year?!"

The drink that came out of the flashy can is white. White from a blue can... Last yearâs coconut flavor was from a white can with a blue interior...

Upon drinking, a mild coconut sweetness spreads across your palate, followed by the tropical mix of grapefruit, lime, and refreshing passion fruitâflavors that are both fruity and invigorating.

Compared to the Coconut Edition (2018 Summer Edition), the coconut flavor is much more subdued, so even those who donât like coconut might find the Beach Breeze blend more palatable.

However, after drinking, thereâs a lingering aroma of artificial air fresheners, fabric softeners, sunscreen, or even perfume, which makes your face scrunch up a bit (-_-;)

You hope itâs some sort of mistake, but as you drink it again, the refreshing fruit flavor is noticeable, yet the fragrance continues to take over, evoking the scent of potpourri...!

Drinking this is like chewing on a potpourriâexactly how you'd imagine the Summer Edition Beach Breeze would taste if eaten directly (ï¼Â´âï½)

With coconut flavor and a slight citrus acidity, itâs ultimately enveloped by the sweet aroma of air freshener. Itâs unclear what they were aiming for. Especially if you drink it at room temperature, the air freshener flavor becomes overwhelming. However, if you chill it well and add plenty of ice, you can enjoy the refreshing fruitiness. Still, some may feel as though they are drinking air freshener, fabric softener, or sunscreen throughout.

Itâs a change of pace from their usual drinkable offerings.

Caffeine: 114mg, Taurine: 1420mg. As always, it contains no fruit juice, and thereâs no special ingredient blend.

In the past, the Summer Editions often offered fruity flavors. The ingredient list might seem simple, but there were deep, enjoyable flavors. This year, however, itâs a bizarre, novelty-like flavor (Î£(Â´âï½ï¼)).

The blue of the can evokes the image of a beautiful tropical island sky and sea, fitting the Summer Edition theme. The color looks great (*Â´è¸ï½*) Itâs a very nice color.

The tab is a silver tab. As has been the case in previous years, the seasonal editions usually become a standard release with a colored tab. So, until then, it will likely stay with the silver tab.

It would be nice to see a beautiful blue tab like the can, but with such a questionable flavor, itâs uncertain whether it will become a regular release... The Americans who tried it seemed to share the same ambivalence as well (ï½).

The can color is great and stands out well in stores, but as a drink, it's hard to predict its future (^_^;).

While consuming a large stock, I decided to compare the Beach Breeze from three countries. From left to right: Canada, Austria, and Germany.

The flavor names differ slightly by country. Having previously compared Yellow Summer (7 countries) and Original (10+ countries) Editions, energy drink enthusiasts like me canât resist doing side-by-side comparisons to see if thereâs any difference in taste.

In Canada, itâs called Beach Blend, in Austria, itâs SÃ¼dseefrÃ¼chte, and in Germany, itâs the same Beach Breeze as in the U.S.

When translated, Austriaâs SÃ¼dseefrÃ¼chte means âSouthern Sea Fruitsââtropical fruits. It certainly would be a perfect tropical fruit flavor if it werenât for that artificial scent.

Comparing them in glasses, the color is the same across all three. The scent doesnât seem to vary either.

Letâs compare the flavors now.

Initially, you might notice some differences in intensity, but after repeated tastings, they all end up tasting the same. With a 750ml bottle, you can enjoy the comparisons leisurely (*Â´è¸ï½*).

While drinking these three, I revisited my earlier âpotpourri flavorâ review and thought, âYeah, thatâs definitely right.â The question of whether you like it or find it unnatural is where opinions will diverge.

The citrusy, fruity, and gently sweet-and-tangy tropical fruit flavor is fine. But personally, I just canât get past the scentâit makes it hard to enjoy (ã½Â´Ï`).

Germany is the only one with its own unique blue tab, while Canada and Austria, like the U.S., feature a silver tab.

The flavor names differ slightly, but the three are essentially the same. Whether itâs worth doing individual reviews for each or combining them into one comparison post, I opted for the latter to avoid excessive reviews.
