name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2019 Gletschereis
description:
This is the 2019 winter limited edition of Red Bull released in Austria, featuring the Gletschereis (Glacier Ice) flavor.

In the following year, 2020, the same flavor was launched in countries outside of Austria. However, the initial release of the Red Bull WINTER EDITION 2019 Gletschereis was the world's first Red Bull with a special can treatment. Let's dive into the review of this unique edition.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, it reveals a clear and beautiful light blue color. This color makes you curious about what flavor it could be. Let's take a sip. Upon tasting, it has a sweet and sour raspberry flavor. There is no fruity taste, just a candy-like artificial berry flavor.

The taste and aroma are somewhat light, with no richness of raspberry fruit, and it tastes like an ordinary berry-flavored candy. Itâs surprising how this flavor could easily be found in inexpensive carbonated drinks, not just Red Bull.

Perhaps the light blue can, which is meant to represent glaciers, was designed to evoke a blue raspberry flavor. However, it doesnât have the typical artificial blue raspberry taste, so Iâm not sure what kind of flavor they were aiming for.

This yearâs Winter Edition has a much cheaper impression compared to the usual high-quality flavors that were released first in Austria.

The light blue color and raspberry flavor donât seem to match well together. I expected a more intricate flavor inspired by glaciers, but this turned out to be just a regular flavor... I was left feeling a bit disappointed.

Caffeine 80mg, Taurine 1000mg.

The light blue and blue combination gives off a cold, icy feel. I didnât expect an ordinary berry-flavored drink to come from a can that looks like this. I feel like the taste doesnât match the color and design, and thatâs disappointing.

At the top of the can, thereâs a snowflake design. This feature is unique to the initial Austrian release and was not included in the worldwide versions that launched the following year.

Additionally, when chilled, the silver-blue of the Red Bull logo changes to blue, which is a major feature of the 2019 Winter Edition available in Austria. As it warms up, it turns to silver, which is a special effect unique to the 2019 Winter Edition in Austria. It was a really nice touch for a winter-themed edition.

The Winter Editions released the following year in other countries, like the US, only had a printed blue logo and didnât have the special temperature-changing design that was introduced in the 2019 Austrian release.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2020 Watermelon
description:
The 2020 Red Bull Summer Edition, Watermelon. Typically released in the US at the end of April or the first week of May, the 2020 edition surprisingly started being sold as early as January.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opening the can, the scent that escapes is a sweet candy-like aroma with no trace of the typical green notes of watermelon. You almost can't perceive the watermelon scent at all. Even if you try to force the scent of watermelon into your mind, itâs a bit hard to do.

When poured into a glass, the color is surprisingly bright red, like a red berry hue. The color is completely different from the usual watermelon flavors that other brands have released, and itâs not what youâd expect watermelon to look like. Those whoâve tried other watermelon-flavored energy drinks may share the same impression.

When tasting it, as expected, the watermelon flavor is quite faint with a sweet, slightly tart fruity candy taste. While thereâs a slight trace of watermelon rind in the aftertaste and aroma, the dominant flavor is sweet candy.

Apple and cherry-like sweet and sour notes can also be detected, and calling it a "watermelon flavor" seems a bit of a stretch. When chilled and the sweetness mellowed out, the watermelon-like flavor became slightly more prominent, but it still feels a bit forced.

Red Bull has previously created excellent fruity flavors without actual fruit juice in many of its Edition series, but this one feels a little off compared to the others.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine. These are simple energy ingredients. In a year when high-caffeine energy drinks are being released by many brands, Red Bull sticks to its usual formula, which I personally appreciate, but I do worry about being left behind by other companies.

The color is similar to the existing Red Edition, but the can surface has a slightly rougher texture. All previous Red Bull cans were smooth, so this change in texture feels new for the 2020 Summer Edition Watermelon. It's unclear if this rough-textured can will be used for future releases. Perhaps this texture was added specifically to distinguish it from the existing Red Edition.

It might be better for Red Bull to switch to more glamorous limited-edition designs like other brands do for seasonal products. With so many Edition flavors being released worldwide, thereâs less room for new colors to be used, and if the color is too similar to an existing product, it loses its novelty. In particular, many color editions are now permanent products in the European and American markets, so the excitement has worn off.

After being released in the US, the 2020 Summer Edition has been launched in several countries.

In Europe, the Summer Edition usually comes out earlier, often before spring, and this year it was released around February, but the US started selling it at the end of January, which was a notable shift.

Even earlier than the US, it was launched in Australia. However, in Australia, it wasn't released as the Summer Edition but as a Red Edition watermelon flavor, starting to circulate in early January. Iâll review the Red Edition separately, so stay tuned.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2020 Sunny Beam
description:
Released in June 2020, the Summer Edition Sunny Beam, a limited edition exclusive to Japan.

While a watermelon-flavored Summer Edition was released worldwide for the summer of 2020, Japan was the only country to release its own exclusive version, the Sunny Beam, also known as the "Golden Red Bull."

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The drink itself was orange. I had imagined it would be a champagne gold similar to the can color until I poured it into the glass, so it felt a bit odd.

Upon tasting, a refreshing pear flavor spreads in your mouth, followed by a sweet and sour tropical fruit mix. The fruity and satisfying flavor doesnât linger too much, and the pear scent is refreshing, making it a perfect summer taste.

According to Red Bull, itâs a "pear & passion fruit" flavor, and I thought the tropical taste would be more dominant. However, the pear flavor was also quite strong, and the unique refreshing mouthfeel and the aroma that fades away after drinking were very pleasant, just as the flavor description suggested.

Since Sunny Beam is a summer-limited product, itâs great even when served chilled with plenty of ice. In fact, it might taste even better this way.

When chilled with ice, the pearâs juiciness stands out, and the passion fruit flavor turns into a clear sweetness, increasing the refreshing feeling. The key is to pour Sunny Beam into a glass filled with ice and drink it before the liquid gets watered down. I wish it had been available in a 250ml can instead of the 185ml one...

Contains 80mg of caffeine, 222mg of arginine, and other ingredients. As with previous editions, this product contains no fruit juice.

Although the "Golden Red Bull" is not exactly a summer-themed design, I personally love this color combination. The main color, gold, contrasts beautifully with the deep burgundy. What really struck me was that the blue, instead of the usual silver, is a more subdued gray. This combination is just amazing (*Â´è¸ï½*)

If it had been silver instead of gray, it wouldn't have had such a calm atmosphere.

Since itâs a limited-edition new product, I bought two cases (*Â´ï½ª`*)

Additionally, the blue on the back changes to a subdued mustard yellow, and looking at the entire can, you can enjoy a color scheme that reflects the beauty of Japan.

By the way, there has never been a Red Bull edition product as colorful as this released overseas in the past.

Recently, Red Bull Japan has continued to release exclusive edition flavors, which is quite unique globally. In fact, Japan and the United States are the only countries where such original products are sold in such quantities.

I hope Red Bull continues to release original products unique to Japan, not just import flavors from abroad.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2021 Dragon Fruit
description:
This is the Dragon Fruit flavor from the Red Bull Summer Edition series, released in the USA in 2021.

Several energy drinks with a dragon fruit flavor have been released before, but since dragon fruit itself has very little flavor, I feel that itâs best to approach it as an "image flavor" when it comes to juices or processed products. Now, let's try the Dragon Fruit flavor made by Red Bull.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a sweet and sour grape-like aroma bursts out. If you open it without knowing it's Dragon Fruit, you might think, "This is grape flavor." Letâs take a sip.

As you take a sip, a light mouthfeel spreads with a sweet and sour grape flavor, along with a hint of kiwi-like taste. The sensation of the seeds in dragon fruit is somewhat similar to the flavor of kiwi, so perhaps this was intentionally replicated.

The fresh, sweet-and-sour taste of the grape flesh, along with the tartness of the skin and a faint bitterness, brings out the deliciousness of the sweet and sour flesh. This change in flavor and depth is a signature feature of Red Bull, even with a fruit flavor that contains no juice.

If we were to evaluate the level of Dragon Fruit flavor recreation, itâs off-mark, so I wouldnât rate it highly. However, as a juice with no fruit juice content that offers a rich grape flavor, itâs very enjoyable.

The flavor itself is bound to appeal to the general public, so it has been decided to be sold as a regular item under the Green Edition after the summer of 2021.

Dragon Fruit was also released in Australia in 2021.

Due to the global lockdown, I was able to visit Australia at the end of 2022. I thought it would be impossible to find the 2021 Summer Edition, but I was lucky enough to discover a store that still had some in stock! In Australia, it had already become the Green Edition as a regular product, so finding last yearâs Summer Edition was truly a miraculous experience.

It contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine. This is a standard amount, the same as in Red Bull Original, with the added bonus of enjoying a rich flavor in the Edition series.

The matte green can feels off for a Dragon Fruit theme, and Iâm left wondering why they chose this color for the first time in Red Bullâs history.

Perhaps they avoided using a vivid red-pink color, which would have been similar to existing Edition cans.

The matte green seems to reference not the fruit of the dragon fruit but the cactus plant itself where dragon fruit grows...

Typically, the vivid red-pink color of the fruitâs flesh is more iconic for dragon fruit, so I think this matte green is an odd choice.

There seems to be a limit to the extent that Red Bull can create flavor imagery through can colors alone, and this was apparent in the 2021 Summer Edition. The mismatch between the flavor image and the can color seems to have become more noticeable.

The 2021 Summer Edition was released worldwide, and just like the American version I reviewed, the âDragon Fruitâ or its alternate name âPitayaâ was sold, while in Europe, it was marketed as âCactusâ due to the fruit being part of a cactus. The matte green color might fit that cactus image better.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2021 Cactus Fruit
description:
The Red Bull Summer Edition 2021, featuring Cactus Fruit, was released in Europe in 2021. This review focuses on the version launched in Germany.

In 2021, Red Bull Summer Edition 2021 Dragon Fruit was released in America and other regions. While Europe didnât explicitly label it as "Dragon Fruit," it was launched with a similar flavor profile under the name Cactus Fruit.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a sweet and sour grape-like aroma with a real fruity sensation bursts out. It's a bit debatable whether this could be recognized as cactus fruit. Let's taste it.

When you take a sip, a sweet and sour grape flavor spreads. It's not purely grape; it has a refreshing and clean taste that doesnât leave a sticky aftertaste, making it easy to drink.

Rather than cactus fruit, the flavor strongly replicates the sweet and sour taste of grape flesh, with hints of acidity and a slight bitterness from the skin, offering a real fruit experience.

The flavor is the same as the Red Bull SUMMER EDITION 2021 Dragon Fruit, released around the same time. In Europe, itâs widely labeled as "cactus fruit," but the flavor seems to be the same as "dragon fruit" worldwide.

Dragon fruit itself doesnât have a particularly distinctive sweetness or sourness, so itâs best to enjoy this as a "concept flavor" that resembles grape.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine.

The matte green color evokes the image of cactus, which is easy to associate with, but it might have been clearer if the color resembled the cactus fruit itself.

Compared to the "Dragon Fruit" version released in North America, the product name and can color donât feel as mismatched, which is a relief.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2022 Strawberry Apricot
description:
Released on April 4, 2022, the Red Bull SUMMER EDITION Strawberry Apricot is a limited summer edition. It feels like the release of the summer edition keeps getting earlier every year...

This year, not just in the United States, but in many countries around the world, the 2022 summer edition featured the same strawberry and apricot mixed flavor.

In the United States, seasonal edition products often become regular items after their limited release, and this time, due to the early release date, it transitioned from the limited edition summer series to a regular color edition called the "Amber Edition" during the summer.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The moment I opened the can, the fragrance reminded me of a tangy strawberry candy and a sweet and sour pomegranate. The color is not a natural fruit type but an artificially colored one. What kind of taste is this going to be?!

When I took a sip, I experienced a mix of the tangy strawberry candy flavor and, indeed, the sweet and sour apricot. Itâs a simple candy-like taste with condensed sweetness and sourness, but it doesnât have the complex fruit flesh flavors or aromas.

I recommend drinking it ice-cold and gulping it down rather than savoring it slowly.

The flavor itself is pretty common, so it might be a nice limited-edition offering, and sure enough, during the summer, the successor product, Amber Edition Strawberry Apricot, was released. It seems like in the U.S., this summer edition was released with the idea that it would eventually become a regular product.

It contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine, which is a standard amount. The Edition series is marketed with the original Red Bull ingredients and offers a variety of flavors to enjoy.

The can has a matte orange finish. It almost looks like the orange-flavored version of Red Bull that was released in Japan.

From the can color, you canât really get the impression of strawberry in the âStrawberry Apricotâ flavor.

This orange seems to be meant to represent apricot.

Interestingly, in many countries outside of the U.S., the 2022 Summer Edition was released with the flavor name in the order of âApricot Strawberry.â Just the order of the words might change the impression of the flavorâs color.

The Edition series from Red Bull doesn't have particularly unique designs, as they focus only on using color to convey the flavor. Iâve been saying for several years now that theyâve reached the limits of using a single color to represent each flavor, and yet, nothing has changed.

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2022 Fig Apple
description:
Released in October 2022, the Winter Edition for the 2022 winter season. This time, it's the Red Bull WINTER EDITION 2022 Fig Apple, which was launched in North America and Europe. (It was released with the same Fig Apple flavor in Canada a year later, in September 2023.)

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening the can, a sweet and tangy, juicy apple aroma with a fruity, fleshy scent fills the air. Let's give it a try. As you take a sip, the sweet, juicy apple flavor is complemented by a subtle hint of La France pear, adding a delicate and fruity note â this is the fig flavor.

The refreshing aftertaste and aroma, which wouldn't be achievable with just apple, come together thanks to the addition of fig. The balance is perfect, with about 70% apple and 30% fig, creating a sweet, mellow taste that brings out the best of both flavors.

With a generous 355ml size, the taste is just right. For 250ml sizes available outside the US, you may find yourself wanting just a bit more, which makes it a perfectly balanced size. The lingering fruit aroma without leaving too much aftertaste is the secret to this deliciousness that makes you crave another sip.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1430mg of taurine. It has no fruit juice, and the energy ingredients are the same as the traditional editions in the series.

Every year, the Winter Edition adopts a more subdued color scheme compared to the regular edition, and this time, the calm green color and matte texture create a wintery feel that makes you want to grab it during the season.

The WINTER EDITION Fig Apple was released in two sizes in the U.S., 355ml and 250ml, while in Europe and other regions, it was released in the 250ml size.

It was fun collecting the WINTER EDITION Fig Apple cans, each reflecting the winter season of different countries. Seasonal limited-edition products are more than just temporary offerings; the importance of capturing the seasonâs mood through design and color became very clear to me. Red Bull releases seasonal editions every year, so next time you're traveling abroad, enjoy the season and the city while picking up Red Bull's seasonal edition for that time.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2023 Juneberry
description:
The 2023 Red Bull Summer Edition released worldwide features a Juneberry flavor. This summer-only product is inspired by berries harvested in early June, and in this review, I will be covering the American SUMMER EDITION 2023 Juneberry.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, a sweet and sour blueberry flavor aroma bursts out. Given that the Blue Edition with blueberry flavor is already being sold, what will this Juneberry taste like? As I take a sip, the sweet and sour blueberry flavor spreads in my mouth. The texture is clear, and the aroma is light and not overly strong, giving it a delicate flavor. The sweetness and umami of sugar are not overly emphasized, so in a way, it has a natural feel.

As a result, after drinking, the blueberry scent lingers slightly, and the aftertaste is light, which is the distinctive feature of the Juneberry flavor.

Personally, I prefer a more complex flavor with a stronger sense of real fruit, so I would go for the existing Blue Edition if thatâs what Iâm after.

In Canada, just like in the U.S., there are two size options: 355ml and 250ml. The 355ml size feels a bit much. I think the 250ml size is the best.

In the latter half of 2023, the product name changed from "SUMMER EDITION" to "SEA BLUE EDITION," and it became a regular item. The quick transition to a regular item suggests that the decision was made beforehand, rather than based on the tasteâs evaluation.

I find it difficult to understand why both this and the existing Blue Edition are sold together, so Iâll be keeping an eye on how both flavors evolve in the future.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine, which is a standard amount for Red Bull.

The can has a matte texture, with bright blue and white text creating a refreshing impression. The design is the same in all countries except the U.S. The silver Bull logo at the top of the can is common to other editions, but the white text of this Summer Edition adds to the overall bright and refreshing impression.

While the SUMMER EDITION 2023 has a clean and refreshing feel, thereâs no real connection between the light blue can color and the actual color of the Juneberry fruit. As Iâve pointed out in previous years, itâs difficult to convey the taste and appeal of the product just through the can color. Over time, many of the easily identifiable flavor colors have been used up, and weâre now seeing more overlap in can colors.

Instead of simply releasing new products with different can colors, it would be better to explore more distinctive designs that convey the unique characteristics of each flavor.

Red Bull once fell behind Monster Energy in the U.S. due to the lack of flavor expansion, and they were also slow to adopt larger-sized cans. Now, I worry that a lack of innovation in design could result in a loss of appeal. Since 2020, especially in the U.S., many new and unique energy drink brands have emerged, so thereâs a high chance that Red Bullâs designs may start to look less distinctive.

By the summer of 2023, both the summer and winter editions planned for 2024 already have their designs locked in, so unfortunately, it doesnât seem like there will be any immediate redesigns.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2023 Mango Pineapple (Japan)
description:
Released on June 6, 2023, the limited summer edition of Red Bull, the Mango Pineapple flavor, available only in Japan.

Released on the same day, this summer edition product clashes head-to-head with the same flavor from ZONe Crazy Vacances . Let's give it a try right away.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, the sweet aroma characteristic of mango flavor fills the air. It's the typical mango flavor profile you often come across. Let's take a sip and find out how it tastes. When I take a sip, I get a refreshing blend of mango and pineapple, with a balanced combination of sweetness and acidity, allowing me to fully enjoy the distinctive flavors of both fruits.

The flavor isn't overly sweet, and the acidity doesn't dominate; the aroma isn't too strong either. It achieves a perfect balance, ensuring neither mango nor pineapple overpowers the other. The aftertaste is clean, with little residue, making it a refreshing drink with a sharp finish.

By the way, when drinking it at a temperature close to room temperature, the sweet mango flavor stands out more. But if it's chilled, it reaches its optimal taste with a perfect mango & pineapple mix.

Adding ice brings out the crisp pineapple flavor, resulting in a refreshing, summer-like taste that is perfect for the season. Both the taste and aroma leave just the right amount of lingering aftertaste, and the refreshing feel of the ice-cold drink truly gives off the vibes of a summer edition.

Personally, I highly recommend it with ice. It turns into a fresh flavor that will transport you to the beach, perfect for Japan's hot and humid summer.

Speaking of the beach, it reminds me of the first Summer Edition I drank at the air race venue beach back in 2016 . Drinking the 2023 Summer Edition, I was once again struck by how great the culture of Red Bullâs âexperienceâ is. The memories from 6â7 years ago came flooding back. As Iâve written in my Twitter profile, "Energy drinks become more interesting with the experience," and this is exactly true.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. Without any fruit juice, it follows the same ingredient structure as the other Red Bull edition series.

With a matte orange and white color scheme, this design gives off a refreshing impression for the summer edition. In Japan, the almost identical orange color was used for the Orange Edition released in 2022. Therefore, there is nothing particularly new about the can color or design, and many people who arenât familiar with Red Bull might not be able to tell whatâs different.

Perhaps because of this, the âNEWâ label was added to this yearâs Summer Edition. This stands out on the simple Red Bull design. I hope this makes it clear that it's a new product and a new flavor.

The previous issue I pointed out in reviews of Japanâs edition series, where the flavor name was often replaced with abstract product names in spots where the flavor should have been, has been effectively resolved. Now, the flavor name is clearly displayed on the front, following the global design. The Japanese text, however, might seem a bit tacky... There are cases where fruit names in English differ from their Japanese names, so it might be tricky to decide whether to use katakana or English. Personally, Iâd prefer English.

Oh, and since the flavor name is now on the front, the phrase ââ¯â¯ Flavorâ that used to be on the back is no longer there.

Red Bull, which uses just color changes for flavor variations, might feel a bit subdued when compared to other energy drinks with flashy designs. While I like this chic vibe, I also hope that the brand can innovate in design.

On June 6, both the ZONe Crazy Vacances and the Red Bull Summer Edition 2023 Mango Pineapple were released. Both are summer energy drinks with the same mango and pineapple flavors. The massive size difference is quite striking. ZONe stands out in terms of cost performance for the same price range. Perhaps Red Bull intentionally released the same flavor on the same day as a competitive move!?

While Red Bull remains a solid player with its original products, I'm curious to see how theyâll respond to competitors with different capacities, prices, and unique designs in upcoming new products.

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2023 Pear Cinnamon
description:
The 2023 Winter Limited Edition of Red Bull is the Pear Cinnamon flavor.

With its warm color typical of winter limited edition products, the combination of fruit and spice has become a staple for Red Bull's seasonal winter editions.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opening the can, a sweet aroma of apple and banana wraps around you. Upon double-checking the product name, I can indeed detect a slightly pear-like fragrance. I believe the cinnamon flavor added has made the scent a bit more subtle and less distinct. As soon as it hits the mouth, a fresh and crisp pear flavor gently emerges, followed by a more pronounced apple-like taste, creating a lively and bright flavor experience.

The cinnamon flavor is barely noticeable, and at room temperature, it leans closer to apple, while chilled, the pear flavor becomes more prominent. When served with ice, the apple taste completely fades, leaving behind the refreshing pear flavor. The flavor is enjoyable even at room temperature, a trait shared by all past Red Bull WINTER EDITION series. Personally, I love this winter-only series that can be enjoyed at different temperatures.

I would be happy if this became a regular offering... but somehow, it seems like the Summer Edition always becomes the staple instead...

While the Red Bull WINTER EDITION 2023 Pear Cinnamon was released in many countries in time for winter 2023, in the Southern Hemisphere, such as Australia and New Zealand, it was released six months later in June 2024 due to the opposite season.

The fresh, sweet, and refreshing aroma of apple and pear is really nice. Thanks to the seasonal shift, I was able to purchase it during my trip to New Zealand in September 2024.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine. These are the standard energy ingredients found in a 355ml can of Red Bull.

The matte wine-red can gives a warm and calm impression, perfectly fitting for winter. The gold used in the flavor name seems to be inspired by the color of pears. The warm-toned can color gives off a rich and relaxed feeling, perfect for the winter season, making you want to enjoy it in a cozy room during a cold winter.

However, itâs a bit concerning that the color is similar to the existing Red Bull PEACH EDITION and even overlaps with past WINTER EDITION cans. The can color choices used by Red Bull seem to have reached saturation, and itâs inevitable that theyâll resemble previous designs.

Looking at the various promotions for Red Bull Edition series, this simple and beautiful design seems to be too perfected, and I donât expect many new designs to surpass it. In the U.S., many new energy drinks with various designs are released every month, and if Red Bull continues to only change the can color, consumers may begin to feel a sense of monotony in the design.

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2023 Muscat (Japan)
description:
Released on October 3, 2023, the Red Bull Winter Edition, a seasonal limited edition, has made its debut in Japan.

While the Winter Edition is released every year globally, this Muscat flavor is the first of its kind and is exclusive to Japan.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. Upon opening the can, a gentle and refreshing muscat grape scent fills the air. The high quality of the aroma raises the expectations for the taste quite a bit. Will it live up to the hype? Let's give it a try! As soon as it touches your lips, a sweet and tangy muscat flavor spreads. The moment you bite into muscat grape flesh, a refined and juicy taste bursts forth.

Even though it's made without fruit juice, it captures the essence of muscat grapes quite well. I encourage you to savor it slowly while reading this review.

The acidity is beautifully enveloped by the gentle sweetness of the muscat grape, creating a realistic flavor and a smooth, drinkable texture. After drinking, a fragrant muscat scent lingers. This results in a flavor that's rich in changes in both taste and aroma, keeping you engaged without growing tired of it.

When drinking with ice, the refreshing sensation is heightened, but the juicy sweetness of the muscat grape can be too overpowering and fade. To enjoy the authentic taste of muscat grape, it's best to refrigerate it.

Although it's released as a winter seasonal product, it still offers a wonderfully refreshing taste that's perfect for the season. Buying it in bulk and enjoying a cold, ice-filled Winter Edition during early summer might be a great idea.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. You can enjoy the muscat flavor while benefiting from Red Bull's signature energy ingredients.

The matte texture and fresh green create a refreshing atmosphere reminiscent of muscat grapes. When holding the actual can, the green color has a more subdued tone compared to the official Red Bull CG imagery, without the intense shine.

At the top right, youâll find the âNEWâ label, which started appearing in the previous Red Bull Summer Edition 2023 . This might indicate that Red Bull will use the âNEWâ label for limited-edition products.

If a seasonal edition proves popular, it can evolve into a color or flavor edition and eventually become a regular product. In Japan, the original Summer Edition became the Yellow Edition.

Personally, I think this Winter Edition 2023 has such a high-quality, refreshing flavor that Iâd love to see it become a permanent product, even for summer.

name: Red Bull Spring Edition 2024 Tropical Pink Grapefruit (Japan)
description:
Released on March 19, 2024, this is the Japan-exclusive, spring-limited flavor of Red Bull Spring Edition Tropical Pink Grapefruit.

Before its release, Red Bull kept the "tropical pink grapefruit" flavor a mystery, generating excitement on social media. What kind of taste has it turned out to be? Iâm excited to dive into the review now!

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening the can, a sweet and sour fruity candy scent spreads. The flavor name includes "pink grapefruit," but neither the scent nor the color really gives off the vibe of pink grapefruit. Let's take a sip and see what it's like. As I take a sip, I get a burst of tropical fruit flavors like sweet and sour passion fruit, papaya, pineapple, and apple.

The pink grapefruit flavor mentioned in the name is only slightly noticeable through its sourness, and it doesn't really stand out. The main flavor is a tropical fruit mix.

If you're expecting a bitter and fresh pink grapefruit flesh taste, you might be a bit disappointed. Personally, I would have liked a bit more of the rich, refreshing bitterness that you'd typically enjoy from a pink grapefruit.

When chilled, both the taste and scent offer a highly satisfying tropical fruit flavor. The aftertaste lingers, leaving a sense of satisfaction. It might be a good idea to enjoy it slowly at a chilled temperature to really appreciate which tropical fruits are being replicated.

Personally, I recommend trying it with ice for an extra refreshing experience. The tropical fruit candy-like taste quickly fades, leaving behind a refreshing aftertaste. I think this is the perfect way to enjoy it as we head into spring and summer.

Itâs unclear if a Summer Edition will be released, but if this tropical flavor is anything to go by, it might be a good idea to stock up for the summer.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. No other energy ingredients are included.

The can features a calm color scheme inspired by rich pink grapefruit flesh, with a smooth, matte finish that gives it a poppy yet luxurious feel. Itâs hard to ignore the slight mismatch between the flavor and can color.

It also features the classic "NEW" mark, a staple for limited edition products released in Japan. Abroad, limited edition seasonal flavors often become regular products, so it will be interesting to see whether this Japan-exclusive Spring Edition will be made a permanent offering in the future.

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2024 Curuba Elderflower
description:
The 2024 summer limited edition, Red Bull SUMMER EDITION 2024 Curuba Elderflower, released in various countries including the United States. This time, it features a combination of the unfamiliar "Curuba" and the well-known "Elderflower" from European energy drinks. What does it taste like?!

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a sweet and sour scent reminiscent of kiwi is released, followed by a smooth, sweet melon-like fragrance. When I take a sip, a tangy passion fruit flavor spreads in my mouth, followed by a refreshing, rich apple flesh taste in the aftertaste. The sweet and sour aroma blends well with the mellow, sweet fragrance, and I can really enjoy the passion fruit and the sweet, floral apple flavor.

What stands out as I drink it is the unique sweet scent, which I believe is inspired by the elderflower. However, it feels more like the rich apple flesh flavor typically found in Japan.

The combination of tangy passion fruit flavor and the rich, refreshing apple creates a unique tropical fruit flavor with a fresh aftertaste, which I find to be highly rated.

I first learned about the flavor name "Curuba" during this review. Upon researching, I found that itâs a South American fruit similar to passion fruit, with a strong sourness. The yellow variety is sometimes called "banana passionfruit" due to its resemblance to a banana. I see now that the strong sourness and passion fruit-like fruitiness I noticed earlier comes from the characteristic taste of "Curuba."

The other flavor, "Elderflower," is commonly found in European energy drinks, and itâs one of my personal favorites. I was excited to see it used for the first time in a Red Bull product, so I was curious how it would taste.

Generally, elderflower flavors are recreated as floral and delicate, but in this case, the sweet and sour taste of "Curuba" takes the lead, and the elderflower essence is more subtle.

That said, itâs precisely because of the elderflower influence that this unique, refreshing, and rich aroma is achieved, setting it apart from other tropical fruit flavors. This release feels like the perfect summer flavor, and I hope it becomes a regular offering.

This is the Red Bull SUMMER EDITION 2024 Curuba Elderflower I tried when I went to Poland in the summer of 2024. It was perfect for the season with its sweet and sour, refreshing floral flavor.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine, which is a standard amount.

The combination of matte green and white gives a refreshing impression.

Red Bull doesnât differentiate the design by flavor, only by color, so itâs a bit disappointing that the products lack distinct features.

It seems that adding silhouettes of elderflower and Curuba to the can itself could make a big difference in its overall look.

This is the best flavor they have ever made in my opinion! Please bring it back!!!!!

name: Red Bull Summer Edition 2024 Lime (Japan)
description:
Released on July 2, 2024, the Summer Edition Lime flavor, a Japan-exclusive and summer-limited product.

This is not a new flavor, but rather a re-release of the limited edition Green Edition, which was launched in February 2021. Now, letâs review the lime flavor for the summer season once again.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. Upon opening, a refreshing lime aroma with a hint of acidity bursts out. Unlike typical lime juices without fruit, this one gives a rich impression of actual lime fruit. Letâs take a sip. When I take a sip, a strong, awakening acidity fills my mouth, followed by the sweet and sour umami of lime fruit. The acidity I feel in the first sip is strong every time I drink it.

The lingering acidity and the high-fidelity lime fruit scent that fades away are in a league of their own, setting it apart from other non-fruit lime flavors.

Since this is a summer-limited Summer Edition revival, I highly recommend drinking it with plenty of ice. In a good way, the umami and any off-flavors fade, and the refreshing lime sensation intensifies, making it easier to drink in large gulps. Additionally, the real lime fruit flavor that pleasantly lingers after drinking is just as enjoyable whether cold or with ice, making me wonder if it was intentionally made to be enjoyed with ice. Pouring it into a glass full of ice creates a refreshing, rich lime flavor.

The aftertaste aroma is exceptional, and once again, I am reminded why the Edition series is so great.

If developing a new flavor incurs significant costs, I donât mind having the same product as those in Europe and the US, especially since it lets people in Japan enjoy flavors that might not be familiar here. So, personally, I think it's a good thing.

For now, I hope the next seasonâs edition brings a new flavor to experience.

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2024 Iced Vanilla Berry
description:
Review of the 2024 Winter Limited Edition Red Bull WINTER EDITION 2024 Iced Vanilla Berry, released in October 2024 in the United States.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When I open the can, I notice a scent of berry tartness coming out, and as I pour it into the glass, a sweet cotton candy aroma fills the air. Once it's in the glass, the berry scent nearly disappears, and the sweet cotton candy fragrance becomes the dominant impression. The liquid color is a cold, glacier-like hue. Now, let's take a sip. Upon taking a sip, I get a blueberry tartness mixed with a lingering artificial aftertaste, resembling gum, while the sweet scent of cotton candy gently wraps around and fades away.

Despite the product name containing "vanilla," I don't really taste any vanilla-like flavor. I suspect that the sweet cotton candy fragrance is meant to evoke vanilla, but it doesn't quite meet the mark of true vanilla.

After drinking, the cotton candy scent gradually settles into a sweet, baby powder-like aroma. I wonder if this is their attempt to bring out a "vanilla flavor" in some way... But, if you're expecting a vanilla taste, youâll be disappointed. The flavor is more of a mix between blueberry gum and cotton candy.

As mentioned earlier, there is no fruit-forward blueberry flavor, just an artificial tartness akin to gum. So, if you're expecting the rich taste typically associated with past Winter Editions, you might find this one underwhelming.

Personally, I imagine how perfect this could have been if it had a creamy blend of vanilla bean's rich fragrance, sugar, milk's depth, and fruity berry flavorsâthis would have been the ideal Winter Edition for a winter-only release. Unfortunately, the product name here was a bit misleading.

To add a note about the product name, it's worth mentioning that in Austria, the 2024 Winter Edition was released under the name "Iced Gummy Bear." With that name, the flavor would align more accurately with the contents, and we likely wouldn't have experienced such a strong sense of mismatch and disappointment.

It contains 114 mg of caffeine and 1320 mg of taurine. No other energy ingredients are included.

In the U.S., it was released in 250 ml and 355 ml sizes. The cold, glacier-inspired light blue color stands out. It's similar to the color of the Red Bull WINTER EDITION 2019 Gletschereis.

While many past Winter Editions have featured warmer hues, do you prefer warm or cool colors for winter-themed Red Bull cans?

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2024 Citrus Orange
description:
This is my review of the limited edition Red Bull Winter Edition 2024 Citrus Orange, which was released on November 26, 2024, exclusively in Japan for the winter season.

This edition is a unique flavor for Japan, unlike the 2024 Winter Edition versions released in Europe, the U.S., and other regions.

In this review, I will also compare it to the similar orange flavor that was released in Japan back in 2022.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Opening the can, a sweet and tangy orange pulp scent immediately escapes. This smells promising! Letâs take a sip. When I take a sip, a fresh and fruity orange flavor bursts with soft sweetness and a hint of tartness, reminiscent of orange pulp.

Thereâs a slight peel sensation, and the aftertaste is refreshing, with the sweet and sour flavor not lingering too long, allowing the juicy orange goodness to shine. Even on a cold winter day, this would be a flavor Iâd want to enjoy chilled.

Itâs a blend of the deliciousness of real orange with the enhanced flavors from sugar and artificial flavoring, creating a flavor that stands apart from cheap orange sodas.

The freshness of the fruitiness and the luxurious orange flavor make this perfect for when you crave a refined orange taste. I think it would be great if this were available year-round, not just as a limited winter release.

I compared the Red Bull Winter Edition 2024 (Citrus Orange) with the Red Bull Orange Edition Sunrise Spark (Iyokan flavor), which was released in February 2022. Since the previous version has been stored for about two years beyond its best-by date, there may be some degradation in both aroma and taste, so this comparison is based on the current flavor profile.

The colors are almost the same. It may be due to the degradation, or perhaps the vitamin B2 in the Winter Edition 2024, but this version looks slightly darker. The scent is also nearly identical. I canât tell much difference; itâs the same sweet, bursting scent of orange pulp. Letâs compare the taste.

The Iyokan flavor is also sweet and sour, with the citrusy orange burst providing a pleasant experience. The base orange flavor in this version is quite similar to the Winter Edition 2024, with both having a citrusy and refreshing orange profile. While the flavor has evolved over the two years, the impression of citrus fruit is still strong.

The 2024 Citrus Orange version enhances the fresh sweetness of orange pulp, with a more balanced acidity, and the umami of the fruit and lingering sweet aftertaste stand out more compared to the previous version.

At first taste, itâs hard to distinguish them, and one might mistake the 2024 version for a re-release of the 2022 flavor. However, the 2024 version emphasizes the sweetness of the orange pulp, while the previous one focused more on the tangy and refreshing notes of citrus.

Both are delicious, no doubt, but the 2024 Citrus Orange has a longer-lasting orange aftertaste, offering a higher level of satisfaction.

This version contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. There are no other energy ingredients included.

The first impression is a refreshing combination of a bright orange and white, giving a calm and subdued feel. Red Bullâs design typically expresses the flavor image through the color and product name alone, which makes it hard to differentiate from past designs.

When compared with the 2022 release of the same orange flavor, thereâs a noticeable difference in color depth.

Additionally, when compared with the Red Bull Summer Edition 2023 Mango Pineapple, the color is almost identical. The color is so similar that itâs hard to tell them apart. This highlights a limitation in Red Bullâs design, which struggles to capture the flavor image or product concept in the design, a challenge that has been apparent for the last 6-7 years.

Since Japan continually releases unique flavors, it would be interesting to see some gradual changes to Red Bullâs overall design, starting with the Japanese editions.

name: Red Bull Spring Edition 2025 Grapefruit & Blossom
description:
This is a review of Red Bull SPRING EDITION 2025 Grapefruit & Blossom, a spring limited release launched in the United States on March 3, 2025.

When I visited the U.S. in early July, store inventories were already nearly depleted, and I was finally able to find a 355ml can at just one store.

Despite being called "Grapefruit & Blossom," the can color is oddly lavender, which feels a bit out of place. However, the flavor itself is exquisite, offering an elegant European character. Letâs dive into the details of the review.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, it releases a fresh, juicy grapefruit aroma combined with a sweet, floral scent reminiscent of elderflower. The fragrance is very similar to the now-standardized RED BULL GREEN EDITION Curuba Elderflower , instantly raising expectations. The liquid itself is an unexpected light green, like young spring leaves. Letâs take a sip.

On the palate, it delivers a juicy burst of citrus fruit flavor, balanced with moderate acidity and a refreshing grapefruit bitterness in the aftertaste.

The sweet, floral elderflower-like aroma enhances the pulp-forward grapefruit flavor, creating a drinking experience where the taste gradually evolves from the first sip to the lingering finishâcomplex and satisfying.

The main grapefruit flavor is incredibly realistic, making it hard to believe thereâs no actual juice. One sip makes you want to grab a second can immediately!

The floral aroma faithfully reproduces a rich elderflower scent, allowing for a natural and enjoyable drinking experience.

In Europe, the product is named "Woodruff & Pink Grapefruit," based on the German herb Woodruff (Waldmeister). This calm aroma is therefore not elderflower, like in the RED BULL GREEN EDITION Curuba Elderflower , but a reproduction of Waldmeister.

Ah, so the green color reflects the Waldmeister inspiration. Hereâs a photo of Waldmeister:

Waldmeister-flavored products are often dyed a deep green, but Red Bull SPRING EDITION 2025 has a gentle, herb-like green, evoking fresh spring leaves.

See all energy drink reviews inspired by Waldmeister here!

Overall, the flavor is calm and sophisticated, perfect for adults enjoying the fresh spring season.

As of July 2025, the product was nearly sold out in the U.S., making it hard to find. Itâs curious that it has not become a permanent item yet. This is an outstanding flavor that deserves permanent release, earning a top rating of 5.

Contains 114 mg of caffeine and 1420 mg of taurine, standard amounts.

The soft lavender color is springlike, but it does not match the flavor, which is a drawback.

The flavor name is printed in a light green matching the drink, but the canâs appearance does not convey the flavorâs appeal.

The Red Bull Edition series relies only on color changes, which unfortunately fails to convey the flavorsâ charm. This particular flavor is so outstanding that itâs disappointing the can design doesnât reflect its deliciousness.

Nowadays, many energy drinks feature packaging that clearly conveys the flavor, and it would delight fans if Red Bull evolved its design to better represent the taste.

We look forward to seeing how the worldâs reigning champion, Red Bull, will continue to evolve.

name: Red Bull Spring Edition 2025 Strawberry (Japan)

Upon opening the can, a sweet and tangy strawberry candy-like aroma bursts out. It doesnât seem to replicate the natural taste of real strawberries very closely. Now, let's take a sip. As I take a sip, a refreshing sweetness spreads across my mouth. Thereâs no artificial aftertaste; instead, it has a mild, soft sweetness with a balanced tartness, reminiscent of strawberry candy.

That being said, it doesnât have the juicy, rich, and fresh strawberry taste either. When served with plenty of ice, the candy-like taste fades, leaving a refreshing strawberry flavor.

The Red Edition Strawberry Apricot flavor, released in Japan in 2022, had a strong impression of a strawberry candy flavor. So, I'll compare it with this new strawberry flavor.

That being said, the Red Edition 2022 has expired by about a year and a half, which means it has likely deteriorated to some extent. Please consider this as a comparison of the flavor characteristics as of 2025. The 2025 Spring Edition is on the left, and the 2022 Red Edition is on the right.

name: Red Bull Winter Edition 2025 Apple (Japan)
description:
Released on October 28, 2025. The Red Bull Winter Edition 2025 Apple flavor is a limited winter edition launched as âJapanâs first apple-flavored Red Bull.â

Red Bull Japan has previously released Japan-exclusive flavors, but for the winter of 2025, it has aligned with the global lineup by releasing a flavor nearly identical to the Winter Edition available worldwide.

name: Red Bull Green Edition Kiwi Apple
description:
The 2016 release of the Red Bull SUMMER EDITION 2016 Kiwi Twist has now been made into a regular product, known as RED BULL GREEN EDITION Kiwi Apple.

The flavor name has been changed from "Kiwi Twist" to the more straightforward "Kiwi Apple."

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When you open the can, a distinctive kiwi-like fragrance bursts out. It's not the smell of real kiwi fruit, but rather the typical kiwi flavor that you often find in energy drinks.

The color is a transparent, calm yellow-green, just like the previous Green Edition that was sold.

When you take a sip, a moderately tangy kiwi flavor spreads. It's not the taste of real kiwi, but rather an artificial taste. There is a peculiar aftertaste that lingers, a characteristic flavor often found in foreign apple-flavored energy drinks. This flavor is somewhat similar to what you find in drinks like Bang Sour Heads and Rockstar Super Sours Green Apple . While it's not the same exact weirdness, there's a certain unappealing taste common in apple-flavored drinks that detracts from their umami and refreshment.

For those expecting the fruity taste of kiwi, this is the complete opposite. It doesn't bring out the sweet-tart flavors you'd expect, and there's a lingering artificial taste that makes it, personally, not very enjoyable.

Since the original Summer Edition Kiwi Twist, I've drunk this Green Edition Kiwi Apple multiple times at room temperature, cold, and with ice, but the artificial flavor has never really changed. Among these, adding ice and drinking it quickly seems to be the easiest way to enjoy it.

By the way, both the 2015 Orange Edition and 2016 Summer Edition Kiwi Twist were flops for two years in a row, lacking any real flavor appeal. Red Bull's Edition series was originally known for creating delicious flavors with no fruit juice, but for some reason, the quality dropped drastically during these two years.

However, in 2017, they made a strong comeback with the Summer Edition Grapefruit Twist , which boasted an incredibly fruity and bitter taste that became one of the best Summer Editions.

It almost felt like the development team completely changed, as the years 2015 and 2016 were memorable failures for me, especially as I would go to America every year to buy the Summer Edition.

Even though the Green Edition has become a regular item, I honestly donât know what to say about it (ï¼Â´âï½)

Caffeine: 114mg, Taurine: 1250mg, with no other notable ingredients. Compared to the Summer Edition, there is a slight difference in the ingredients, with the Green Edition reducing the daily Vitamin B6 percentage from 360% to 350%. Aside from that, I couldn't find any significant differences in the ingredient list, and there were no noticeable taste differences.

As with other seasonal editions that became regular, the flavor and contents of the Green Edition have hardly changed. But Iâll leave a review comparing them.

The color is exactly the same, and I didnât notice any difference in the fragrance. Looking at this color, youâd think, "Kiwi & Apple flavor! Can't wait!" but... the taste doesnât quite match my personal preference (^_^;)

Comparing them, the Summer Edition leaves a stronger peculiar aftertaste, while the Green Edition seems a bit more enjoyable now that itâs become a regular product. However, after alternating between them, I realized the flavor hasnât changed at all.

It would have been interesting if there had been a flavor difference, but as expected, thereâs no difference between the seasonal and regular editions.

The Green Edition is sold in both America and Europe, but the flavor is the same as the original American version, so Iâll skip that here. Personally, I donât like the Green Edition, but I think many people in Japan might be disappointed by the peculiar aftertaste and lack of fruitiness. If you get a chance to try it, I suggest savoring it slowly.

name: Red Bull White Edition
description:
The 2018 Summer Edition Coconut Berry Flavor became a regular product, now known as Red Bull WHITE EDITION. In this review, Iâll be checking out the White Edition I brought back from Austria.

After the 2018 Summer Edition was discontinued, the regular product was given names like "White Edition" or "Coconut Edition" depending on the country, but the contents are the sameâa mix of coconut and berry flavors.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, the mellow sweet scent of coconut fills the air. Those who aren't fond of coconut may feel repelled as soon as they open the can.

The drink itself is a bright light blue. Itâs the kind of color youâd expect from an energy drink, right? The slight cloudiness might be trying to capture the essence of coconut.

The coconut doesnât bring much of a distinctive sweetness; its scent is more prominent. The main flavor is a refreshing mix of sweet and sour fruits like apple, berry, and plum, which I personally find quite delicious. Did coconut really need to be in here...? (ï¼Â´âï½)

The refreshing fruit mix flavor is tasty enough on its own, so those who dislike the scent of coconut might find this drink disappointing. Itâs likely that some people would enjoy it if the coconut aroma wasnât there.

Originally released as the 2018 Summer Edition, I thought, âThereâs no way this will become a regular product,â but to my surprise, it became a staple worldwide. Even though itâs now a permanent offering, I think itâs a taste thatâs still divisive, so if you get the chance, give it a try. Itâs sold in many countries around the world.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine, which are the standard ingredients for a 250ml can of Red Bull. By the way, there are no fruits or coconut ingredientsâit's completely fruit juice-free.

The all-white can with the silver bull is simple and elegant. Thereâs no other edition quite like it. White and silver generally give the impression of a sugar-free product, but what do you think? Those familiar with energy drinks, like our friend Drin-Kun, would know that White Edition is not sugar-free from the get-go.

By the way, sugar-free editions are marked with the sugar-free label and a diagonal silver stripe.

Aside from the White Edition, thereâs also a Coconut Edition available. The product name differs depending on the country, but the contents are the same. While thereâs no need to do a side-by-side comparison, I did try comparing the White Edition and Coconut Edition, so feel free to check it out. On the left is the White Edition from Austria, and on the right is the Coconut Edition from Australia. The country names can be a bit confusing!

Both have the same coconut-scented fruit mix flavor. Even after drinking a total of 500ml (two cans), the coconut aroma never grew on me, and I didnât find it any more enjoyable. However, if you love coconut water or the taste of coconut itself, this might be a drink you'll really enjoy.

name: Red Bull Yellow Edition (Japan)
description:
In Japan, the first Red Bull Summer Edition was launched in 2015, and later, in 2018, it became a regular product as the Yellow Edition.

Since its release, Yellow Edition was only available at select stores, so it wasnât widely known. However, around 2020, it began appearing in some nationwide chain drugstores, making it more accessible to the public.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The color of the drink is a transparent yellow, without any fruitiness. Since the Red Bull Edition series contains no fruit juice, thereâs surprisingly little emphasis on cloudy appearances.

Upon sipping, a sweet and tart tropical fruit flavor of orange, lemon, and pineapple spreads. The pleasant acidity and unique tropical fruit aroma are complemented by a Japanese-inspired yuzu flavor, making it a smooth citrus fruit mix thatâs easy to drink (à¹Â´Ú¡`à¹).

Considering how delicious it is, 250ml seems a bit small. Itâs been 7 years since I first drank it in the U.S. when it was released in 2014, and the 355ml size in the U.S. is definitely the right choice. Delicious 250ml cans like this often disappear before I even realize it while writing reviews.

Despite its incredible flavor, itâs curious that itâs only sold at select stores. It would be great to see it alongside the regular White Edition, offering more variety and helping people discover the deliciousness of the Edition series.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. The ingredients are quite standard, and I appreciate the brand not engaging in the over-the-top caffeine content race.

The yellow can with âYellow Editionâ is straightforward and easy to understand. At first, when the Edition concept was still new in Japan, it received some cold comments like âRed Bull, but yellow?â But, itâs now one of the longest-selling Red Bull products in Japan.

The flavor is clearly marked as âTropical Fruit.â After this, Red Bull Japan began using more abstract product names, making it harder to know the flavor just by looking at the front of the can (although they later changed it to include specific flavor names).

For more details, check out past reviews of the Fresh Breeze , Sunny Beam , and Refreshing Splash . The "Tropical" label is a great way to know the flavor even before buying it, which I think is very helpful.

Here are the different versions of the Yellow Edition series released in Japan. Starting with the Summer Edition, it transitioned into the Yellow Edition with two variations.

The contents didnât change, but there were some updates to the labeling rules, which led to the creation of the third generation.

In April 2024, the design of the Edition series was updated with a white, circular Red Bull logo, marking the 7th generation of the Yellow Edition design.

This logo first appeared on the Red Bull Summer Edition 2023 Mango Pineapple released on June 6, 2023. It was originally used to mark new products, but when it became a regular product, the Red Bull logo without the "NEW" mark was added to the Edition cans.

It does feel a bit confusing, but it seems that without the noticeable Red Bull mark, the Edition might not be recognized as part of the Red Bull series by the general public. However, after 10 years of Edition releases in Japan, I hope this wonât be the case.

When the Yellow Edition was first released in 2018, it was sold only in select restaurants, internet cafes, and university co-ops. I remember going to TGI Fridays to try it, but it was already out of stockâ¦ I left disappointed, recalling my American-style meal.

Now, it seems to be available at drugstores like "Welcia," "Tsuruha Drug," and "Kusuri no Fukutaro." With the price drop for Red Bull, it has become more affordable, and I hope it will expand to more convenience stores and supermarkets nationwide.

name: Red Bull Tropical Edition
description:
In Europe and other regions, the Yellow Edition is sold under the product name "Tropical Edition." This time, I will be reviewing the Tropical Edition sold in the UK.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a burst of sweet and sour tropical fruit fragrance fills the air. If you've had the Yellow Edition before, this scent alone will definitely boost your excitement. When you take a sip, the mild acidity brings out a refreshing tropical fruit flavor. A mix of pineapple, mango, orange, and papaya creates a beautifully recreated tropical fruit essence, even without fruit juice. This is undoubtedly one of the best-tasting cans in the Red Bull Edition series.

The Yellow Edition is also available in Japan at this link , but the flavors in Japan and abroad are slightly different. Be sure to try both the Tropical Edition and Yellow Edition when overseas.

Contains 80mg of caffeine, 1000mg of taurine. These are typical amounts for energy ingredients.

Personally, I prefer that the UK version is labeled as "Tropical Edition" rather than "Yellow Edition." Itâs much clearer, and itâs better to know the flavor right from the product name. The flavor name is carefully repeated as "Tropical Fruit Flavor," which is a common feature of the Edition series. This helps make the flavor easily recognizable even before opening the can, making it more approachable.

Although there is nothing particularly new about this long-selling product, itâs easy to understand why it has remained a beloved classic. Drinking it brings back memories of searching for the limited-edition Los Angeles flavor released in 2014 (the first-ever release of Red Bull's tropical fruit flavor in America). I hope you enjoy the tropical fruit flavor while experiencing the thrill of hunting for energy drinks locally.

name: Red Bull White Edition Fresh Breeze (Japan, Limited Edition)
description:
Released on March 3, 2020, the Red Bull White Edition Fresh Breeze is a limited edition flavor, marking the first new flavor in Japan in four years (it was later re-released in a 250ml size and became a regular product in 2021). It has a refreshing peach flavor. *As of January 2023, the 250ml size of the White Edition has been removed from the official website, and discounts are appearing online. It seems to be discontinued.

Overseas, the White Edition has already been released as a regular product, and in 2019, the Peach Edition was released in the U.S. Hereâs a review comparing those flavors as well.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a rich peach aroma reminiscent of canned peaches or peach nectar bursts out. The scent is stronger than expected.

When poured into a glass, the drink appears cloudy white, the exact color you would imagine for white peaches.

As it touches your mouth, a refreshing sweetness spreads with a lively, juicy peach flavor. Despite its light texture, the rich peach aroma gives a satisfying experience.

The aftertaste fades almost entirely, leaving no stickiness or residue. A subtle peach aroma lingers, surprisingly realistic, offering a lingering aftertaste like youâve just eaten fresh peach flesh. I'm always impressed by how this edition achieves this without using actual fruit juice.

Itâs not an overly punchy flavor, but the strong aroma and moderate peach sweetness make the 185ml mini can clearly insufficient...

âI think this should be released in 250ml!!â I thought, but refreshing it as a quick drink is also a nice option. When served with plenty of ice, the peach sweetness becomes even more refreshing and delicious (à¹Â´Ú¡`à¹).

Initially a limited product in 185ml, the White Edition became a regular product starting December 1, 2020, with the price remaining the same. As I mentioned in my review, 185ml was simply too small, and the price was a bit steep. Many people, Iâm sure, didnât feel like buying it at Â¥200 for the mini size.

Now, with the 250ml size priced at Â¥200, I hope more people can enjoy Red Bullâs exceptional peach flavor.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 222mg of arginine, the same as regular Red Bull. Even with the 250ml size, the caffeine remains at 80mg, but the arginine content increases to 300mg. This difference is negligible in terms of sensory experience.

As indicated on the can, White Edition Fresh Breeze is a limited-time release. (It was upgraded to a 250ml size and became a regular product in 2021!) Once itâs gone from store shelves, itâll no longer be available, so if you love the rich and fresh peach flavor, I recommend buying in bulk. *Now, with the 250ml size and as a regular product, you can enjoy Red Bullâs peach flavor anytime ( Â´âï½)bï½¸ï¾ï½¯!

By the way, the White Edition is not a limited product worldwide; itâs available as a regular item. These are some of the summer editions, White Edition, and Coconut Edition available worldwide. Interestingly, the overseas White Edition was originally a seasonal limited product, âSummer Edition 2018 Coconut Berryâ , but it was made a regular product and continues to be sold as the White Edition (or Coconut Edition, depending on the region) in Europe and other areas.

The overseas White Edition features a coconut scent and a fruit-mix flavor, which is completely different from the Japanese peach flavor.

Now, letâs compare the global White Edition with the Japanese White Edition. On the left is Japanâs White Edition (Fresh Breeze), and on the right is the globally available White Edition (Coconut Berry). This time, Iâve compared it with the German White Edition.

The blue from the coconut stands out strongly. The blue color of the product is matched with the liquid inside, while Japanâs White Peach maintains a color that reflects the peach theme. Looking at the comparison, I think Japan might have benefited from a more striking pink color. At the same time, the blue from the coconut flavor feels too artificial, creating a bit of an awkward contrast.

Japanâs Fresh Breeze has a refreshing peach flavor, while the overseas Coconut Berry offers a coconut and tropical fruit mix, with a more distinctive coconut aroma that might be a bit polarizing. Personally, I prefer Japanâs peach flavor and feel a bit disappointed that it's a limited edition.

Before the 2020 release in Japan, letâs compare the Japanese White Edition with the Peach Edition that was released in the U.S. in 2019.

In 2020, not only the 355ml size but also the 250ml Peach Edition was distributed throughout the U.S. Personally, I find the 250ml size too small (ï¼Â´âï½)

The color of Japanâs White Edition is clearer. The U.S. Peach Edition is cloudy, and you canât see the bottom of the glass. When comparing the taste, both offer the same peach flavor, and youâd hardly notice the difference if you didnât do a side-by-side comparison.

The U.S. version has a stronger sweet-and-sour flavor, and the lingering peach aroma is more intense. Overall, it offers a rounder peach sweetness.

On the other hand, Japanâs White Edition also delivers a solid peach sweetness but feels fresher and more transparent compared to the U.S. version.

Thereâs no clear winner or loser hereâboth are incredibly well-made, offering a satisfying peach flavor.

There are a few aspects where I think Japan could have improved its design. Letâs take a look at the can design. As for the product name, âFresh Breezeâ alone doesnât tell you what flavor it is. Meanwhile, in the U.S., itâs simply called the âPeach Edition,â and the can clearly labels âPeach Nectarine,â making it much more recognizable.

Many Japanese still donât realize how delicious energy drinks can be when theyâre made with fruit juice flavors. Using an abstract name like âFresh Breezeâ doesnât give much of a hint about the flavor, so something like âWhite Peachâ might have been more straightforward. Energy drink brands often use abstract names in Japan, but I think it could be clearer.

From the 185ml release to the 250ml standardization, many non-sale boxes have appeared.
