name: Red Bull Purple Edition
description:
Red Bull's Acai-flavored drink, PURPLE EDITION. After the release of the Summer Edition in Brazil, it was launched in various countries under the names ACAI EDITION and PURPLE EDITION.

The one I'll be reviewing today is the PURPLE EDITION released in Germany.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When you take a sip, the sweet and sour flavors of grape and blueberry spread in your mouth. While it doesn't have a real fruitiness, it doesn't taste overly artificial either. It feels like the sweet and sour umami of grape and blueberry is the main highlight.

The taste isn't heavy or rich, but the strong aroma ensures that the blueberry flavor lasts throughout, providing a high level of satisfaction.

Itâs easy to drink with no unpleasant aftertaste, and it's so delicious that you might find yourself finishing a 250ml can without realizing itâdefinitely a challenge for anyone writing a review Î£(Â´âï½ï¼). PURPLE EDITION is so stable that it's almost hard to find a flaw.

PURPLE EDITION doesnât have a particularly addictive taste or a strong impact, but it has a stable and delicious flavor that makes you want to reach for it. It's the kind of taste you won't get tired of, no matter how many cans you drink in a month. Thatâs important!

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine. This is a standard Red Bull energy blend.

A purple Red Bull is something we haven't seen before. The color gives it a calm, premium feel. In Japan, the âgrape flavorâ Blue Edition was released, but the can wasnât purple. If that version had been released as PURPLE EDITION, it would have been quite a breakthrough! (^_^;)

Europe, in particular, has a wide variety of established editions, and you can enjoy colorful Red Bull no matter which country you visit.

Itâs not a flavor you savor and sip slowly, but when you grab it from the fridge on a whim, youâll find yourself thinking, âWow, this is delicious,â and finishing it in one go. If you see it in Europe, make sure to grab a few cans to bring home.

name: Red Bull Purple Edition (Japan)
description:
The Purple Edition of Red Bull, released on June 8, 2021, is a limited edition product.

Previously, the Acai-flavored Summer Edition was released in Brazil, followed by the Acai Edition in various countries. It was later released as the Purple Edition. The version released in Japan features a unique grape flavor.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

True to its name, the Purple Edition is a beautiful purple color. A sweet grape scent wafts through the air. Upon tasting, you can feel the sweet and tart fruitiness of the grape. There's no chemical aftertaste, and at 250ml, it's easy to finish in one go because of its deliciousness.

The balance of the grape's sweetness and tartness is just right, allowing you to enjoy the refreshing taste of the fruit flesh. It's a rich grape flavor typical of Red Bull.

Even with ice, the grape's umami doesnât weaken and can still be enjoyed, with the fruitiness giving a fresher impression, making it highly recommended!

The fact that you can enjoy this flavor without any fruit juice is one of the highlights of the Red Bull Edition series. Unlike previous editions that were often left unsold, this one disappeared from store shelves quickly, and before you knew it, it was gone.

The Blue Edition, released in Japan in October 2015, had a grape flavor. Despite being the Blue Edition, it was a unique flavor exclusive to Japan. Since the new Purple Edition is also a grape flavor, I decided to compare the old and new Red Bull grape flavors.

On the left is the Purple Edition, and on the right is the Blue Edition. After six years, the Blue Editionâs color has completely faded and turned a smoky gray. Itâs cool in its own way, but when I poured it into a glass, I was shocked. It's not uncommon for the color to fade over a few years, like in Rhinos Relaxation .

So, I tried the comparison. However, as I mentioned, there was no real need to compare, as the taste of the Blue Edition has deteriorated, and the characteristic sweetness of the grape was lost Î£(Â´âï½ï¼)

Although the grape scent and tartness remain, the grape flavor no longer holds up. Upon tasting the new Purple Edition, I felt that the old Blue Edition was very similar to it, but the deterioration over six years was much more advanced than I had imagined, making it impossible to do a proper taste comparison. This canât be helped. I just wanted to share with you how the grape flavor from a few years ago faded and turned color like this.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. All Edition series products have the same energy ingredients and proportions as the original. Recently, caffeine content has been increasing in Japan, but in terms of total daily caffeine intake, this amount seems just right.

And every time, I'm impressed by how delicious this is without any fruit juice. Iâve always wondered what Red Bull would be like if they made a fruit juice-based product.

The can is entirely purple, with a silver line at the top, creating a combination of purple and silver that gives it a calm, luxurious feel.

The uniquely Japanese "Mystic Magic" on the can doesnât make it obvious what the flavor is, but with a purple Red Bull, you can probably imagine the flavor just by the can's color. *On March 7, 2023, the design was changed to include the flavor name, and it became a regular product. Please check the details below.

The worldwide Purple Edition includes the "Acai" flavor name, but Japan sticks to its unique approach of not including a flavor name. (^_^;)

Originally released in limited quantities in 2021, the Purple Edition was suddenly re-released as a vending machine exclusive on March 29, 2022.

The label that once said "Limited Edition" is gone, and it seems to have become a regular product. As a fan, itâs great to see this!

The Purple Edition quickly disappeared from stores, so I had to buy boxes of it on Amazon, and I drank them all up quickly... I was too cautious, so when it became a regular item, the timing was perfect!

As always, the umami of the grape flesh is so refreshing. The Edition series of Red Bull is different from the usual grape flavors, so I hope youâll take the opportunity of this re-release to taste it again.

*By the winter season of 2022, the Purple Edition had disappeared from vending machines.

The Purple Edition, which disappeared from vending machines in the winter of 2022, made its return as a regular product on March 7, 2023. I'm personally thrilled about the Purple Edition becoming a regular item, especially considering it has one of the best flavors among Japan's Edition series!

Until now, Japan had a mysterious name where the flavor should have been listed, making it hard to imagine the taste, but with this return, the flavor is clearly labeled as "Grape Flavor." Globally, this can be seen as a step toward standardization. In previous reviews of Japanâs Editions, I mentioned that itâs better to clearly show the flavor name on the front, and the Purple Edition has finally made this a reality. I hope future Edition series releases also have flavor names clearly displayed.

name: Red Bull Açaí Edition
description:
The Summer Edition that was released in Brazil has now become a staple product, known as the ACAI EDITION. It is now available not only in Brazil but also globally as the ACAI EDITION and PURPLE EDITION .

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opening the can, a subtle berry scent wafts out, but it doesn't come across as overpowering.

When I take a sip, the first impression is a slightly sweet, mildly tart grape flavor. The taste evolves into a blueberry scent and aftertaste, offering a gentle sweet-and-sour grape & blueberry flavor. If you're expecting the clean and natural taste of acai, you may be surprised by the more robust punchy flavor of grape and blueberry.

This drink has no fruit juice, offering a sweet-and-sour berry flavor that isn't particularly distinctive, with no off-putting aftertaste or cheap flavors. It's a fairly basic, enjoyable taste that anyone can easily drink.

The Acai Edition is perfect for refreshing yourself in the morning. The natural, easy-to-understand grape flavor is delicious and straightforward, and the 250ml can is just the right size for it.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine. It shares the same energy ingredients as regular Red Bull, with no fruit juice added.

With so many different flavors now, I think it would be great if each could have unique ingredients to match their taste. However, Red Bull has consistently stuck to its standard blend.

A purple Red Bull, which we've never really seen before. Even though there was a "grape flavor" released in Japan, it was strangely the Blue Edition back then. It was a great idea for the Acai Edition to come from Brazil, the birthplace of acai. It would be great to see more Red Bull flavors based on the characteristics of different countries.

Now, the Acai Edition is available in many countries outside of Brazil, sold as the Acai Edition or Purple Edition. The taste itself isn't anything particularly special, but I don't think many people would find it bad. It's one of those editions that I hope will continue as a staple product for a long time.

I happened to have both the Acai Edition and Purple Edition, so I decided to do a comparison of the three flavors. From left to right: the Acai Edition from Brazil, the Acai Edition from Australia, and the Purple Edition from Germany.

Thereâs no noticeable difference in color. Red Bullâs contents are mostly the same across regions, unless specific changes are required by local regulations.

I couldn't find any difference in this Acai Edition either. The well-balanced sweet-and-sour grape and blueberry flavor is best enjoyed chilled without ice.

Although thereâs a total of 750ml across the three cans, I didn't get bored at all while slowly sipping them during the review. Normally, drinking that much at once would make me tired of the flavor, but that wasnât the case this time.

The Acai Edition isnât so amazing that I'd call it "irresistibly delicious," but this comparison made me realize that itâs a reliably good and stable flavor that appeals to a wide audience. (*Â´ï½ª`*)

name: Red Bull Peach Edition
description:
Released in 2019 in the US, the Red Bull Peach Edition was launched without going through the seasonal edition process.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

From the rich-colored can comes a cloudy, light white liquid. Before pouring, I thought it would be a darker yellow.

When I took a sip, the flavor was mildly sweet, with a refreshing peach flavor accentuated by a slight tartness. Surprisingly, it was an easy-to-drink flavor that seemed tailored for general consumption, particularly for Japanese people.

Given that this is from America, I had imagined it would be richer and more tart, but the soft, sweet aroma of peach gently envelops the drink, making it smooth and easy to drink without being overpowering. The aftertaste is light and clean, without lingering, and the lingering fragrance is pleasant, giving it surprisingly good depth.

Personally, I like the taste, but if you're expecting a punchier peach flavor more typical of energy drinks, you might be a little disappointed as it's too mild.

While drinking a few cans during work, I noticed it has no strong aftertaste, and thereâs no awkward flavor or strong "wow, this is amazing!" feeling. Itâs just very drinkable as a daily beverage. It doesnât get boring either.

It contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine. As usual, it follows the standard Red Bull energy formula.

The main colors are maroon and yellow, with a combination of colors that give off a Japanese, traditional feel. Until the release of Peach Edition, most of the Red Bull cans used silver as the main color, so this edition stands out with its unique presence.

Unlike Japan's pink peaches, this design may reflect the red-ripe skin and juicy yellow flesh of an American peach. By the way, Japan's juice "Nectar" and "Nectarine" are completely different things. The fruit in this picture is a nectarine. It looks delicious! (*Â´è¸ï½*)

Previously, Red Bullâs standard sugary drinks usually became a regular product after being released as limited seasonal editions, so when Peach Edition was announced, I found it a bit strangeâwhy was it coming out now?

I think Japanese people would enjoy the flavor, but I'm not sure how well it's received in America. I had initially thought that the Peach Edition would be a little too mild for Americans, lacking the punch they might expect, but it has remained a regular product without disappearing.

Personally, I believe that if it had been released as a sugar-free version with stronger aromas, it would have fit the target audienceâs taste and needs even better. Iâm sure that a sugar-free version would still offer a refreshing flavor thatâs just as enjoyable as the sugary one.

name: Red Bull Red Edition Watermelon
description:
The new Red Bull RED EDITION with a watermelon flavor was released in Australia in January 2020.

Later, in the United States, the 2020 Summer Edition was launched in early February with a watermelon flavor, and in 2021, the Red Edition in the U.S. switched to the watermelon flavor, which was also adopted in various countries around the world.

â» In Japan, the RED EDITION was released as a limited edition in 2021. â Review of Red Bull RED EDITION Wild Passion

â» For some reason, in Japan, the RED EDITION was renewed in 2022 with a strawberry flavor. â Review of Red Bull RED EDITION Groovy Fizz Strawberry Flavor

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The color is bright red, fully colored. Itâs easy to imagine that itâs not a natural watermelon flavor from the color alone (^_^;) Upon tasting, a sweet fruity flavor with a sour kick spreads across your mouth, reminiscent of the "Suika Bar" ice cream.

While it may not be the most authentic watermelon flavor, the scent is very familiar to Japanese people, as it resembles the "Suika Bar" ice cream, so you can easily imagine it as "kind of watermelon, no wait, this tastes like Suika Bar." Itâs a little artificial in flavor, but since watermelon flavor is always hard to become juicy and savory, this canât be helped.

When you drink it with plenty of ice, it truly tastes like a Suika Bar flavor. Itâs just delicious (*Â´è¸ï½*) In many Western watermelon-flavored products, there is often a grassy scent added to represent the "melon" aspect of the watermelon, but this Red Bull version doesnât have that, which makes it easy for Japanese people to drink without any sense of discomfort.

Starting in Australia, this new watermelon-flavored Red Edition has spread to the U.S. and Europe, becoming the new standard for Red Edition. Goodbye cranberry flavor, and hello watermelon flavor!

Contains 80mg of caffeine, 1000mg of taurine, and no fruit juice.

The design is the same as the previous Red Editions, with the words "Watermelon Flavour" written in green, which resembles the skin of a watermelon, and thereâs no difference from the previous Red Edition. It might be time for Red Bull to change the design for each flavor. Having a watermelon silhouette would make it more fun for fans.

And in the case of a renewal like this, some people might end up buying it without noticing the flavor change in the Red Edition.

name: Red Bull Green Edition (Japan, Limited Edition)
description:
The Red Bull Green Edition, a limited edition product released on February 2, 2021, features a refreshing lime flavor that gives you a cool, invigorating feeling, perfect for summer. True to its description of "Refreshing Splash," it offers a refreshing taste that youâll want to enjoy during the warmer months.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, the refreshing lime fruit scent bursts out, building anticipation even before taking a sip. When I take a sip, the sharp tangy taste provides an intense and punchy sensation, but it quickly transforms into a fresh, sweet and sour lime flavor, letting me fully enjoy the distinct lime taste.

The tanginess doesnât linger too long, and the lime aroma and sweet-sour flavor stay refreshingly on the palate, making it a perfect flavor for a refreshing experience. Itâs so delicious that I end up finishing the 250ml can in no time (à¹Â´Ú¡`à¹).

While the lime aroma is outstanding, the fruitiness and texture are not too intense. It tastes like a lime candy with a refreshing and juicy feel. Itâs enjoyable both chilled and over ice. The lime aroma is strong, so even with plenty of ice, the lime flavor doesnât get diluted, and I can gulp it down while savoring the lime flavor. Itâs a flavor thatâs perfect for the summer.

Contains 80mg of caffeine, arginine, and no fruit juice.

The smooth matte texture of the can gives it a high-quality feel. This texture is something new that hasn't been seen on Japanese Red Bull cans before. The Japanese Green Edition features a lime flavor, unlike the kiwi-flavored Green Edition released overseas in 2017. The can is in a distinctive deep green color, different from the overseas Green Editions. As stated on the top of the can, itâs a "Limited Edition," so once it sells out, itâs gone. If you love this delicious and flavorful edition, itâs best to secure a few cans early.

The flavor name is written as "Refreshing Splash" in white on the can. It might have been easier to understand if it just said "Lime."

Actually, overseas, a lime-flavored "LIME EDITION" was released separately from the Green Edition in 2015, and the limited edition Green Edition available in Japan is an adaptation of that product. By the way, the overseas LIME EDITION has already been discontinued. If you line up the Japanese Green Edition and the LIME EDITION from around the world, you can clearly see how different the green hues are.

While lime flavor itself is quite common, itâs clear that the can design sets this product apart from the lime-flavored Red Bull products released previously.

Japan has released limited edition flavors and designs unique to the country in the past, and this Green Edition is another example of a "Japan-exclusive Green Edition."

Itâs a fresh, invigorating flavor that makes you want to drink it in the summer, and I think it would also be delicious as a mixer with alcohol. It would be great if this lime edition became a regular summer item. It's a shame itâs limited to a certain number of cans.

While browsing Twitter, I saw many comments saying that the Green Edition tastes like Sprite. I can see why people might think of Sprite since itâs a lemon-lime soda.

Personally, I thought the Green Edition was on a different path from Sprite, even though itâs also a lime flavor, so I never associated it with Sprite. So, I decided to do an unusual taste comparison between an energy drink and a regular soda. This might be the first time on Energy Drink Mania!?

On the left is Red Bull Green Edition, and on the right is Sprite. The Green Edition has a murky, fruit-filled color, while Sprite is clear and refreshing.

Since Iâve already written a lot about the Green Edition in my review, I decided to try Sprite. It has a smooth mouthfeel, a mild sweetness, and a faint lemon-lime aroma, with a subtle tanginess. Thereâs no fruitiness or zest, and itâs a clean, refreshing soda. Although both are lime-flavored, itâs clear that the Green Edition is a different experience.

On the other hand, the Green Edition has a rich, tart lime taste and aroma that stands out, and the aftertaste is slightly bitter with some acidity. After drinking Sprite, the Green Editionâs lime flavor feels much more intense and fruity.

Interestingly, Sprite, with its less intense lime flavor, contains 1% fruit juice, while Red Bull Green Edition contains no fruit juice, as expected.

When drinking the Green Edition alone, I felt that it was a refreshing lime flavor perfect for summer, but after the comparison, I realized that Sprite is much clearer and more refreshing, making you want to drink it all at once. In comparison, the Green Editionâs lime flavor is much more intense and rich.

The label also says "Sweet and Refreshing," but the lime flavor is much clearer and more refreshing than the sweetness.

Many people have commented that the Green Edition "doesnât feel like an energy drink," which is unfortunate. The flavor and aroma are well-defined and shouldnât feel out of place globally. But I guess Red Bull Japan is probably chuckling at that (^-^;)

name: Red Bull Red Edition Wild Passion
description:
Released on September 28, 2021, as a limited-edition flavor, Red Bull Red Edition Wild Passion.

The product name, "Wild Passion," makes it hard to guess the flavor before trying it, but those who have read reviews of overseas energy drinks will probably have a good idea of what the flavor might be just by looking at the design!

Letâs dive in and see what the Japanese version of the Red Edition tastes like.

â»In Japan, for some reason, the Red Edition was renewed in 2022 and a strawberry flavor was released. â Red Bull Red Edition Groovy Fizz Strawberry Flavor

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The contents are rich and deep red. A watermelon-like scent wafts from the glass. When you take a sip, it tastes like a candy version of the sweet and tangy watermelon popsicle, but more intense. Itâs a bit hard to say if it's exactly watermelon, but the unique watermelon scent lingers after drinking, so you can faintly feel the watermelon essence.

The sweet-tart taste is stronger than the fruitiness of watermelon, so some might think it tastes more like a berry-flavored or sour strawberry drink.

Even if you savor it carefully, it might still be hard to pinpoint the exact flavor, but Red Bull helpfully lists the flavor name on the back of the can. After checking this, you might think, "Yeah, thatâs probably what it tastes like." Without this info, it might be hard to identify it as watermelon flavor.

By the way, this watermelon flavor is not exclusive to Japanâitâs a global flavor. In the past, Japanâs Red Edition has had unique flavors, so this global flavor release is a rare occurrence.

That being said, since this watermelon flavor has been released worldwide since 2020, I compared the overseas versions with the Japanese limited-edition Wild Passion.

In January 2020, the Australian version was released first, followed by the American version as a summer edition in March 2020, and the Japanese limited-edition watermelon Wild Passion came out in September 2021.

From left to right: America, Japan, and Australia.

The color of the contents is the same in all versions, and the scent seems to be indistinguishable. Letâs try them. The flavors are all the same sweet-tart candy taste with a watermelon-like essence. The Australian version feels a little more sour and refreshing, while the Japanese version is slightly sweeter than both the American and Australian versions, but the difference is minimal.

There were no noticeable flavor differences that would lead to a strong preference for one over the others. Even the sugar and calorie contents in each country show only minor differences, so you can enjoy the same watermelon flavor wherever you go.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. Standard energy ingredients, along with Red Bullâs usual non-fruit juice formulation.

The can is designed with a matte red finish and a green accent, evoking a watermelon theme. This color scheme is consistent with the newly released Red Editions worldwide. The flavor name, "Wild Passion," is written in an abstract way unique to Japan, adding an element of mystery and fun as you try to guess the flavor before tasting it.

Interestingly, most Red Bulls abroad list the flavor name on the packaging, so you have a better idea of what to expect before drinking. Even with the flavor name, itâs still exciting to wonder, "What does a watermelon-flavored Red Bull taste like?" since the taste, aroma, and chemical notes can vary significantly depending on the brand.

By the way, the overseas Red Edition used to be a cranberry flavor and was a long-time bestseller. Many might have tried it abroad before. Even though itâs non-fruit juice, the cranberry flavor was wonderfully balanced, and it was discontinued in 2020 in favor of the new watermelon flavor. Now, this watermelon Red Edition is available in many countries.

name: Red Bull Orange Edition Sunrise Spark
description:
Released as a limited edition on February 1, 2022. The Japanese version of Red Bull Orange Edition, Sunrise Spark.

The flavor of the Orange Edition released in the U.S. and other countries wasn't impressive, but the Japanese version stands out with its unique Iyokan citrus flavor.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening the can, a refreshing citrus scent fills the air. Right away, I could tell this was different from the Orange Edition released overseas. The international versions of the Orange Edition were somewhat disappointing in terms of flavor... When you take a sip, a pleasant tartness and refreshing orange pulp flavor fill your mouth, offering a citrusy taste that is very much characteristic of Japan.

Unlike the artificial juice taste of the overseas Orange Edition, this Japanese version features a more authentic citrus orange flavor, making it a uniquely Japanese flavor. Honestly, the international versions had a cheap taste that didn't feel like Red Bull, but the Japanese version delivers the flavor of real orange pulp, and I personally rate it highly.

The "deliciousness that feels like it has juice, even though it doesn't" is one of the signature qualities of the Edition series, which has been released every year in the U.S. since 2014. I believe the Japanese Orange Edition faithfully reproduces this quality.

This time, it is an "Iyokan flavor." The sweetness is restrained, and it doesnât linger too long on the tongue. The tanginess and slight astringency perfectly capture the essence of Japan's Iyokan citrus. By the way, the Japanese Yellow Edition has also been modified with yuzu to create a unique tropical flavor, and itâs delicious too, so I recommend you try it as well.

The Orange Edition was first released in the U.S. in 2016, a whole six years ago (and frankly, it wasnât that great). If it had tasted exactly like the original, I would have been thoroughly disappointed.

Red Bull Japan did a fantastic job of localizing the orange flavor, which can often be cheap-tasting, and made it into a high-quality product, staying true to the deliciousness of the Edition series. Iâm excited to see what new products they will release in the future.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. Itâs free from fruit juice. The caffeine content isnât too high, so thereâs no need to worry about overconsumption.

The Japanese version of the Orange Edition features a matte finish, which gives it a premium feel, much like the Edition series releases in recent years. As this is a limited edition, the can has the "LIMITED EDITION" line at the top. The flavor name area also includes the uniquely Japanese abstract word "Sunrise Spark."

Hereâs a comparison of the Orange Edition from the U.S., Japan, and Italy. Itâs not obvious in the photo, but when compared to the glossy surface of the overseas Orange Edition, the matte finish adds a touch of luxury to the silver parts. The "Sunrise Spark" section on the Japanese can isnât silver but white, making it stand out against the orange background.

Japanese Red Bull is often thought to come in smaller sizes, but the Edition series is typically 250ml, with the 355ml size only available in North America. The charm of the Edition series is to enjoy its unique flavor in this limited quantity. As the Japanese Orange Edition is a limited release, I recommend securing it early if you enjoy the taste.

name: Red Bull Ruby Edition Vivid Flash
description:
Released on April 26, 2022, the Red Bull Ruby Edition. This time, thereâs no âlimited editionâ label on the canâs top, but based on the press release online, it seems to be a limited-time offering.

Upon picking it up and checking the flavor name on the back, I found it says "Mangosteen Flavor"! Unlike the version released overseas in 2017, which had a different flavor, this is a Japan-exclusive Ruby Edition with a unique flavor.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The color of the drink is a cloudy white, resembling the flesh of mangosteen. A sweet and refreshing aroma spreads out. Let's give it a try.

Upon sipping, the refreshing sweetness of mangosteen, peach, and lychee, with a slight tanginess, creates a fruity and full-bodied taste. The aroma and changes in sweetness and acidity replicate the flavor of mangosteen flesh quite well. Thereâs no chemical taste commonly associated with energy drinks, making it enjoyable for everyone. This gentle flavor seems to target women.

Mangosteen, often referred to as the "queen of fruits," isnât widely consumed in Japan. If you havenât tried the Ruby Edition yet, you might find it reminiscent of peach or lychee flavors, which are more familiar.

Japanâs Red Bull has already released a peach-flavored White Edition, a Japan-exclusive flavor, so this edition gives a similar vibe. The two flavors do overlap a bit.

When served with ice, it becomes even more refreshing, and the tropical mangosteen flavor can be enjoyed with an extra crispness. Personally, I recommend drinking it ice-cold in large sips.

This edition contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine, a standard energy composition for a 250ml can. With these levels, you donât have to worry about drinking too much, so you can enjoy it without stress.

A matte texture with a subtle luxurious feel and a vivid ruby color gives the Red Bull a bold look.

The design of the can perfectly mirrors the ruby-colored outer skin of the mangosteen and its white flesh inside. I really enjoy these kinds of visual representations.

In 2017, an overseas version of the Ruby Edition was released as a summer limited edition and later became a permanent flavor, with a pink grapefruit flavor.

So, the Japan Ruby Edition, with its mangosteen flavor, is an exclusive release for Japan.

The overseas pink grapefruit version was incredibly delicious, and I thought we might get to enjoy it in Japan too. If it had arrived in Japan during summer, it wouldâve been amazingâ¦

On the Japanese version, the flavor name appears as "Vivid Flash" in white, standing out prominently.

At first glance, the can doesnât reveal the flavor, so anyone familiar with the overseas Summer Edition or Ruby Edition would be surprised to find out itâs actually a mangosteen flavor.

The back of the can clearly states "Mangosteen Flavor."

If you look at the past Japanese editions, youâll notice that Japan often features unique flavors, different from those in other countries. While this is great for trying something new, it also means that we donât get to experience some of the delicious flavors available overseas. It's a bit frustrating at times. (^_^;)

From the press release, it appears that the Ruby Edition is once again a limited-time release, but unlike previous editions, the can doesnât feature the "limited edition" label anymore.

Despite being limited edition, the Red Edition and Orange Edition still have stock left on store shelves. When products linger too long, the âlimited editionâ feel fades away.

The Ruby Edition has a flavor close to the White Edition, and the can color resembles the Red Edition, which was released in 2021. While I love the vibrant ruby color, it lacks the sense of novelty that would make it stand out in stores. Will the Japan Ruby Edition become popular?

In a campaign on the official Red Bull Twitter account, 1,000 people can win the "Glimmering Wings Kit."

Opening a box resembling a fortune-teller's box, youâll find...

Inside, thereâs a Ruby Edition can, an original can, and dice.

It seems like you roll the dice to decide what to do next. Red Bull often creates fun and exclusive items like this, which is always interesting to see.

name: Red Bull Ruby Edition Pomegranate
description:
Released as a limited edition product during the winter season of 2022 in Australia, the RUBY EDITION Pomegranate is a unique flavor compared to the previous RUBY EDITION releases in Japan and Europe. It features the same pomegranate flavor as the 2021 Winter Edition in the USA .

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a sweet and tangy aroma of pomegranate, cherry, and acerola fills the air. When you take a sip, the cherry flavor hits with a nice balance of sweetness and tartness. The strong tang typical of pomegranate is not present, and if the product didnât have the pomegranate label, most people would probably identify it as a cherry flavor. Itâs a superb flavor that combines the richness of cherry fruitiness with a smooth, easy-to-drink profile.

The deep sweet-and-tart taste of cherry is subdued, but the full cherry flavor combined with the strong fragrance offers a very satisfying taste experience. The balance of flavor and aroma makes it particularly pleasant to drink.

While the pomegranate flavor isnât particularly strong, the sugar-coated cherry taste and the slight aftertaste of cherry fruit flesh are impressively well done. Itâs such a high-quality flavor that itâs almost a shame itâs a limited edition.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine. These energy ingredients match the standard Red Bull formula.

The can has a smooth, matte finish and a deep red-purple color that gives it a luxurious feel. As with other global edition series, the flavor name is prominently displayed on the front of the can, making it easy to identify the flavor at a glance.

I compared the same RUBY EDITION product released in Japan. Although both are red in color, they have a completely different vibe. The Japanese version has no flavor indication, making it unclear what flavor it is. This is a cringe-worthy design that seems to only exist in Japan. Many people have probably forgotten what the flavor even was by now.

The RUBY EDITION Pomegranate released in Australia is the Australian version of the WINTER EDITION Pomegranate that was released in the USA in 2021. When placed side by side, you can see the cans have the same color. Thereâs a sense of calm, along with a feeling of luxury and warmth.

In Australia, this was released not as a seasonal limited edition, but as a color edition from the start. Nonetheless, it was still a limited quantity product.

By November, when winter season was over, most stores had already sold out of stock. In Australia, where V Energy Drink and Red Bull are overwhelmingly dominant, I recommend securing limited-edition products early.

name: Red Bull Green Edition Dragon Fruit (Cactus Fruit)
description:
Released in March 2022, the 2021 Summer Edition has become a permanent addition to the lineup. While the dragon fruit flavor isnât an exact match for the real fruit, the fruity taste is still delicious and ranks among the best of the past editions.

With the release of Red Bull GREEN EDITION Dragon Fruit, the RED BULL GREEN EDITION Kiwi Apple , which had been available since 2017, has been replaced by the new Red Bull GREEN EDITION Dragon Fruit.

Similarly, the flavor released in Europe in 2021, Red Bull SUMMER EDITION 2021 Cactus Fruit , has also become part of the Red Bull GREEN EDITION lineup. Although the flavor name is "Cactus Fruit," it has been reviewed here as "Dragon Fruit" under the same review.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When you open the can, a fruity grape scent bursts out. The real grape flavor I experienced in last year's SUMMER EDITION has made a return, and I can immediately feel the excitement from the aroma. Letâs take a sip.

Upon tasting, the sweet and sour, authentic grape flavor spreads. The delicate balance of sweetness and sourness is gentle, allowing you to enjoy the fresh, juicy taste of grape flesh.

Furthermore, a slight acidity and faint bitterness contribute to the realistic taste of the grape skin. Despite being a juice-free product, the richness and authenticity of the fruit flavor make this one of the top flavors in the Edition series, which has become a permanent product.

Although the flavor is named "Dragon Fruit," itâs debatable whether it truly tastes like dragon fruit. This is because dragon fruit itself doesnât have the distinct sweet-sour flavor typical of other fruits. The flavor in this GREEN EDITION is best enjoyed as a dragon fruit-inspired taste.

When it was first released as a seasonal product in 2021, I knew it was bound to become a permanent product due to its outstanding flavor. Iâm thrilled to see that it has become permanent not only in the US but also in many other countries, including Europe. Now, you can enjoy this flavor all over the world, so be sure to try it if you're traveling abroad.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine.

The design remains the same as the 2021 Summer Edition, with a renewal into the Green Edition.

The red-pink color represents the fruit, yet, curiously, it's in a green can for the "GREEN EDITION."

It seems the design was inspired more by the green of the cactus rather than the actual dragon fruit.

It might have been better to align the can color and product name more closely with the flavorâs image. However, I believe the limitation of using color alone to represent flavors has already been reached about 4-5 years ago, so I hope for a design change soon.

Since Red Bull rarely misses in terms of taste, it would be great to see the can design evolve to reflect the high quality of the flavor as well.

This is the Red Bull GREEN EDITION Owoc Kaktusa that I picked up during my trip to Poland in 2025. It features a sweet and tangy burst of fresh blueberry and grape pulp flavors, delivering a rich taste accentuated by the sweetness of sugar.

name: Red Bull Blue Edition Ocean Blast
description:
Released on July 19, 2022, this is the third time the Red Bull Blue Edition has been launched in Japan, and it features a new flavor. It might be a bit hard to understand, but Japan has had the Blue Edition released three times now Î£(Â´âï½ï¼)

As you can tell by the can color, unlike the overseas Blue Edition with blueberry flavor, this version is a lychee flavor unique to Japan. Letâs dive in and see how theyâve captured the lychee taste.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening, a sweet lychee fragrance spreads out. The drink has a cloudy white color, typical of lychee-based beverages. The fragrance and color make it easy to imagine the taste. When I take a sip, I get a faintly sweet and sour lychee flavor. It has a smooth sweetness that doesn't linger too long and a gentle acidity that adds a nice touch to the overall flavor.

Lychee itself isn't particularly strong in flavor, so this may differ from the rich and bold flavors typically expected from Japanese energy drinks. While there's no need to overly process the lychee flavor for an energy drink, this Blue Edition might be considered, for better or worse, a bit too ordinary in taste.

This kind of flavor is nice to enjoy cold for a solid sweetness, but personally, I prefer it with ice to enhance the refreshing feel and enjoy the lychee aroma.

Red Bull Japan often releases similar flavors, like the White Peach in the White Edition, the Mangosteen flavor in the Ruby Edition , and now this lychee flavor in the Blue Edition. It seems like they tend to push these refreshing flavors.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine, which are standard energy ingredients for Red Bull. There are no special ingredients unique to the Blue Edition, and like previous editions, it contains no fruit juice.

The new summer release comes in a bright turquoise blue. The matte texture gives it a refined look. This turquoise blue is unique to Japan for the Blue Edition.

Letâs take a look at the three different Blue Editions released in Japan. The globally recognized Blue Edition released in Japan in the past included the first blueberry flavor in 2014 and the second Japanese-exclusive grape flavor in 2015. This lychee-flavored Ocean Blast is the third version of the Blue Edition.

The color is a bit too bright to be considered typical Blue Edition. Even Red Bull officially calls it "New light blue Red Bull!", but "Light Blue Edition" would be too long, so this is probably the best choice. Perhaps "Ocean Edition" might have been a better name?

In September 2023, the product name "Ocean Blast" on the front of the can was discontinued, and the flavor name "Lychee Flavor" was clearly labeled instead. Typically, the flavor name should be clearly stated on the front of the can, which is the global standard. However, Japan had the product name, which wasnât related to the flavor. This change was made in September 2023, in line with the Purple Edition 's shift to being a regular store item, resulting in the change to flavor names for other existing products.

Given the feedback about the unclear product names in other reviews, I think this more straightforward labeling is a good change.

Incidentally, the product name "Ocean Blast," which evokes the image of summer at the sea, is similar to the 2019 seasonal limited summer editionâs name, "Beach Blend" and "Beach Breeze" . These are part of the global summer-themed product lineup, following a similar naming convention.

Although the flavor of the overseas 2019 summer edition had a slight coconut flavor and was tropical with a sunscreen and air freshener taste, unlike Japanâs Ocean Blast, the can design and product name have similarities with this Japanese Blue Edition. The beautiful ocean blue, with its white lychee flavor, makes the "Blue Edition" yet another uniquely Japanese product. However, it also resembles the color of the 2019 Summer Edition released worldwide, which might cause some confusion. Personally, I would prefer to see a more globally recognized flavor with a clearer product name, rather than following the Japanese-exclusive route.

name: Red Bull Red Edition Groovy Fizz (Japan)
description:
Released on September 27, 2022, this marks the second Red Edition in Japan. According to the official description, the flavor is "strawberry." It is quite unusual for the same color edition to be released globally within a year.

Though the product is called "Red Edition Groovy Fizz" in Japan, upon picking it up, the flavor is actually the same "Strawberry & Apricot" from the 2022 Summer Edition . This flavor has now become the Amber Edition in the U.S. as a regular offering.

Is Groovy Fizz really Japan's unique strawberry flavor? Letâs try it out and find out!

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When you open the can, a sweet and tangy aroma reminiscent of strawberry juice or strawberry candy fills the air. The color of the drink also reflects that strawberry vibe.

Taking a sip, you get a sweet and sour strawberry candy flavor. While it doesn't offer a fresh fruitiness, the rich taste is definitely enjoyable. For an energy drink, itâs a pretty acceptable option.

Personally, the candy flavor is a bit overpowering...

So, when you add ice, the strawberry flavor becomes fresher and the candy-like taste is less intense. At room temperature or refrigerated, it may feel a bit too strong. But with ice, itâs the perfect balance for a refreshing gulp.

If you check the back of the can, the official press release states the flavor is "strawberry," but it actually says "Strawberry & Apricot."

This is the same flavor as the 2022 Summer Edition released globally, which has now become the Amber Edition in the U.S. Letâs compare them and see for ourselves.

Iâve already reviewed the 2022 Summer Edition . Now, Iâll compare it with the Amber Edition I picked up during my recent trip to the U.S.

On the left is the Japanese Red Edition Groovy Fizz, and on the right is the U.S. Amber Edition.

Both have the same color, and the aroma is identical. If you shuffle the glasses, you wouldn't be able to tell which is the Red Edition Groovy Fizz.

When you taste them side by side, the Japanese version feels slightly richer, with a stronger sweet and sour strawberry candy flavor. However, there is no difference in the base flavor; both Japan and the U.S. versions share the same taste and aroma. Either way, youâll enjoy the same strawberry candy-type flavor. Of course, both are recommended with ice.

The product name and colors differ, but the taste is the same.

If you follow Red Bull Japanâs claim of "strawberry flavor," the Japanese Red Edition makes it easier to picture the taste with its red color.

It contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. The energy ingredients are the same as regular Red Bull, and it is made without any fruit juice.

The can has a red matte finish, and at the top, there is a subtle orange label stating "New Flavor." This orange-yellow hue may symbolize not just the red of strawberries, but also the yellow and orange tones of apricots.

In previous editions, this area featured the "Limited Edition" label.

This time, it says "New Flavor" for the initial release, but after some time, itâs likely to become a regular product with a fully red Red Edition, as per the press release.

Given that this release came just a year after the Watermelon Wild Passion release, it makes sense that they would label it as a "new product/new flavor."

Looking at the Red Edition cans side by side, the color difference is immediately noticeable. However, when you look at just one, it may be hard to tell the difference. This could be especially confusing for people who don't regularly buy energy drinks.

The orange can design, used overseas for the Strawberry & Apricot flavor, is similarly confusing. The red and light orange combination might be a bit of a compromise.

If Japan were to release the Amber Edition, the strawberry candy flavor might seem somewhat nonsensical, especially considering Japan had previously released the Orange Edition .

As Iâve mentioned in previous reviews, using an abstract product name like "Groovy Fizz" instead of a specific flavor name makes it even more confusing. If they had used "Strawberry & Apricot," as in the overseas versions, it would have been clearer to consumers.

For example, just adding "Watermelon" to the previous Watermelon Wild Passion Edition would have made the difference between the two editions much clearer.

That said, the "Groovy Fizz" name and the official website design both suggest that this is inspired by "groovy, musical vibes."

The campaignâs catchphrase is "The Wings of a Beating Heart," and theyâve even created limited-edition record-shaped merchandise. Itâs a cool idea!

Still, if you look at the product alone, it just looks like the classic Red Edition. I wish the design could better reflect the music culture behind it.

description:

You can enjoy the richness of blueberry flesh, along with a slight tartness and a hint of bitterness from the fruitâs skin, but the flavor doesnât get too overwhelming. The balance of the intensity and the pleasant aftertaste allows you to enjoy both the deliciousness of the blueberry fruit and the refreshing drinkability.

When revisiting it after it became a regular item from a limited summer edition, I once again realized how itâs the perfect fresh blueberry flavor for the summer season, and the 355ml large size provides just the right amount of drinkability.

That said, itâs a bit unclear if it stands out enough from the already available Red Bull BLUE EDITION, so one of them might be discontinued soon...

It contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine, which is a standard amount.

The matte texture, along with the summer sea-inspired light blue color, mirrors the design of the Summer Edition 2023 , and the product name âSEA BLUEâ fits this theme perfectly. In the United States, it is available in two sizes, 250ml and 355ml, just like previous editions.

Right after the launch of the SEA BLUE EDITION in the U.S. in 2024, I found a promotional refrigerated display in stores. Seeing these types of displays during overseas trips right after a new release brings a unique excitement.

name: Red Bull Pink Edition Wild Berry
description:
This is a review of Red Bull PINK EDITION Wild Berry, which began rolling out in select regions in January 2025 and was officially released across the United States on March 3.

In various European countries, a sugar-free version of the same flavor was launched in 2024, marketed as "PINK EDITION Forest Fruits" in the UK and "SPRING EDITION Waldbeere" in Germany.

In the U.S., it wasnât released as a seasonal edition. Instead, like in the UK, it was introduced from the start as a permanent item under the color edition line, "Red Bull PINK EDITION." Now, let me dive right into the review.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When I open the can, a juicy aroma of sweet-tart mixed berries like raspberry and cranberry bursts out. Despite being the Pink Edition, the liquid itself is a reddish-purple just as the flavor suggests. Now, let me take a sip. As I take a sip, a bright, tangy raspberry flavor spreads across my palate. The richness from the sugar enhances the berry fruitiness, and together with the acidity, it creates a well-balanced and consistently enjoyable taste. It delivers a classic mixed berry flavor.

A moderate fruitiness and a sugar-heavy cherry punch character coexist in almost equal measure, resulting in that familiar, no-juice mixed berry taste.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1320mg of taurine.

A fully pink Red Bull had only appeared once before with the Red Bull Spring Edition released in Japan in 2016, but it reappeared in various European countries in 2024, and in 2025 in the United States with this release Iâm reviewing.

Consumers in each country were likely surprised to see a pink Red Bull they had never encountered before. However, this pink appearance may not clearly convey the image of a sweet-tart berry flavor.

As Red Bull has released many flavors over the years, it seems to have reached the limit of expressing product identity through color alone since around 7â8 years ago. As Iâve mentioned before, the Edition series likely needs a fundamental design overhaul.

name: Red Bull Green Edition Curuba Elderflower
description:
Released in November 2024, the "Red Bull SUMMER EDITION 2024 Curuba Elderflower," which debuted in the U.S., has already become a regular offering, and today Iâm reviewing the RED BULL GREEN EDITION Curuba Elderflower.

The previously available "Red Bull GREEN EDITION Dragon Fruit" was discontinued with the launch of this new RED BULL GREEN EDITION.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening the can, a sweet and tangy aroma of apple and kiwi, along with a smooth, sweet fragrance, escapes. Having already tasted it in summer, the enticing smell makes me eager to drink it. Let's take a sip. When I take a sip, the sweet and tangy juiciness of apple, the fresh acidity of passion fruit, and a smooth, mild flavor that I believe is inspired by elderflower, all blend together in a refined and delicious way!

The floral, mellow aroma reminiscent of elderflower is a standout feature. Elderflower is often used in energy drinks across Europe, so it's wonderful that we can now enjoy this distinct European flavor in North America and other countries.

The elderflower flavor here is more subtle compared to other European products, and it enhances rather than overpowers the tropical fruit flavor of "Curuba."

"Curuba," known for its yellow appearance and flavor, is also called "banana passion fruit." The fruity taste with a refreshing passion fruit-like acidity likely comes from the "Curuba" flavor.

The combination of this exotic tropical flavor and the calm elderflower makes me very happy that this summer-exclusive product has been made a regular offering in the U.S. and will continue to be available there.

It contains 114mg of caffeine and 1420mg of taurine, which are standard amounts for energy drinks.

The matte lime green and white font color create a very fresh impression. The flavor name is in contrasting orange, giving it a tropical vibe.

This RED BULL GREEN EDITION is a regular product based on the 2024 U.S. Summer Edition released that same year.

Until 2024, the U.S. had been selling the same-named "Red Bull GREEN EDITION Dragon Fruit," which was just being phased out around the time I bought this new version in the U.S. In the fridge, you can see the 2024 Summer Edition on the left, the soon-to-be-discontinued Red Bull GREEN EDITION Dragon Fruit on the bottom left, and the newly released RED BULL GREEN EDITION Curuba Elderflower on the right.

I love taking photos like this that capture the perfect timing of product transitions, and itâs one of the joys of energy drink collecting.

Iâve placed the old and new Green Editions alongside the Summer Editions. Both Green Editions were originally released as summer exclusives and have now become regular products. Both flavors are so good that itâs impossible to say one is better than the other. Thatâs why itâs a shame that the Dragon Fruit flavor will be discontinued. Even though both are called "Green Edition," they look so differentâwhy did they have to share the same name?

This is the limit when using color names to represent a wide range of flavors. There was once a similar yellow-green "RED BULL GREEN EDITION Kiwi Apple." I've been writing about the limitations of using color to describe flavors for 5 to 6 years, and unfortunately, this trend seems set to continue beyond 2025.

Incidentally, in Austria, the Curuba Elderflower has been made a regular offering under the name "Lime Green Edition," and the Dragon Fruit Green Edition is still being sold alongside it. I would have liked the same to happen in the U.S., but perhaps Dragon Fruit didnât sell well there.

name: Red Bull LIME Green Edition Curuba-Holunderblute
description:
The 2024 summer limited edition released in Austria has been made a regular product under the name Red Bull LIME GREEN EDITION.

In the United States, the largest market for energy drinks, the previously available Red Bull GREEN EDITION Dragon Fruit has been discontinued and replaced with the new Red Bull GREEN EDITION Curuba Elderflower . As a result, the Dragon Fruit flavor has disappeared from the U.S. market.

Meanwhile in Austria, the Dragon Fruit flavorânow discontinued in the U.S.âis still available, and the 2024 summer edition has been introduced as the Lime Green Edition, allowing both to be sold side by side. Since both are among the most delicious Red Bull flavors, this approach is highly commendable.

Incidentally, the 2024 summer edition has also been made a regular product under the name "Lime Green Edition" in Belgium and Spain. In countries like the Czech Republic, Ireland, and the UK, it has been regularized under the name "Green Edition," just like in the U.S.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

Upon opening the can, you're greeted with a burst of fresh and tangy citrus aroma, followed by a rich, sweet fragrance reminiscent of elderflower. Just from the scent alone, you can already tell it's going to taste amazing. Letâs give it a try. As soon as it touches your tongue, a mix of sweet and sour flavors like orange, passion fruit, and apple spread across your palate, gently enveloped by the soft floral notes of elderflower.

This fruity blend is said to recreate the taste of âCuruba,â a fruit also known as banana passionfruit and native to South America. As described above, several fruit flavors are intricately blended, creating a refreshing and fruity drinking experience. The delicate and calming aroma of elderflower adds a smooth, relaxing finish that keeps the tropical notes from becoming too overpowering.

I usually try to avoid sugary drinks, but the satisfying sweetness and elegant fruity flavor of this one keep me coming back for more. Among the recent edition series, Red Bull LIME GREEN EDITION stands out as one of the highest-quality flavors.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 1000mg of taurine. No other energy ingredients are included.

The main color is a refreshing lime green, paired with vivid orange flavor text that evokes the juicy flesh of the Curuba fruit. Since âLIME GREEN EDITIONâ has more characters than can comfortably fit on a 250ml can, I imagine there was some debate over what name would be most appropriateâwhether to go with a color edition or a flavor edition.

This photo was taken during my energy drink hunt in Vienna, Austria, in the spring of 2025. You can see both the Green Edition on the left and the new Lime Green Edition on the right displayed side by side.

In countries like Austria, Belgium, and Spain, both versions are being sold simultaneously by branding the new product as âRed Bull LIME GREEN EDITIONâ instead of discontinuing the existing Green Edition. Thatâs definitely a welcome move!

In many other countries, however, one or both versions have been discontinued.

Perhaps the concept of Curuba and elderflower wasnât easy to convey in some markets? If the can design had incorporated a more visual representation of Curubaâs juicy pulp or the essence of elderflower, things might have turned out differently. The current minimalist design based solely on color coding feels like such a missed opportunity.

name: Red Bull Green Edition Muscat (Japan)
description:
This product is the permanent version of Red Bull Winter Edition 2023 Muscat , which was introduced as a limited edition on October 3, 2023.

It is a flavor that beautifully captures Japanese elegance, freshness, and the complex umami of muscat grapes. In my review at the time, I even concluded by saying, âI sincerely hope this becomes a regular edition,â as it left such a strong impression. That wish has finally come true.

By the way, the 2023 Winter Edition reportedly recorded the highest repeat purchase rate in the history of Red Bull Editions in Japan.

After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, a sweet, tangy, and juicy aroma of muscat grapes bursts out. The quality of the aroma is exceptionally high, making it immediately clear that this is a muscat flavor with a rich, fruity character. Now, letâs give it a try. As soon as I take a sip, a light mouthfeel spreads with the sweet and tangy umami of muscat grapes.

Although the taste itself is light, the muscat flavoring is quite robust, giving it a real, juicy, and floral muscat fruit flavor that lingers refreshingly.

The reason the previous edition became the No.1 in repeat purchase rate in the history of Japanese Editions might be due to the perfect balance of the rich muscat fruitiness and a refreshing aftertaste that doesnât linger, creating a flavor that everyone can enjoy.

Now that I try it again, I find no noticeable flaws, and the way the muscat flavor is so accurately reproduced that anyone could recognize it immediately is truly Red Bullâs strength.

Limited-time flavors are delightful, but I feel that having something delicious available anytime is even better.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine. You can enjoy the muscat flavor along with Red Bullâs standard energy ingredients.

A beautiful matte green that expresses the shimmering, fresh young grass color reminiscent of muscat grapes. Combined with the white font color, it has a clean and elegant finish.

Here it is lined up with the Winter Edition released in 2023. Itâs exciting to see a Japan-exclusive flavorâone that doesnât exist overseas and is truly exquisiteâbecome a permanent edition. A special Red Bull that can only be found in Japan will likely also appeal to international visitors.

In 2025, Europe has introduced Lilac Edition and Peach Edition, both permanent versions of seasonal editions, so it feels fitting for Japan to have Muscat Edition. Over more than 10 years, countless Color Editions have been released, and the pool of âcolorsâ usable as product names is nearly exhausted. Going forward, we may see the naming shift toward âFlavor Editionsâ as the new standard.

name: Red Bull SUDACHI EDITION (Japan)
description:
This is a review of Red Bull Sudachi Edition, released on July 14, 2026 as a new summer flavor.

Overseas, this flavor was released as the Sudachi Lime flavor of the 2026 Summer Edition, a seasonal summer release. In Japan, however, it was introduced not as a limited seasonal edition, but as a permanent product under the name "Sudachi Edition."

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

On the palate, a sweet-tart and refreshing citrus flavor gently spreads, creating a sensation as if the fruitiness is soaking in smoothly. Although there is a slight lingering finish, both the sweetness and acidity remain clean and natural, resulting in an easy-drinking experience. The citrus profile is reminiscent of the refreshing yuzu flavor from the discontinued Japan-exclusive Yellow Edition . Compared to the original Yellow Edition, Sudachi Edition has a softer mouthfeel with a more balanced acidity, which is one of its defining characteristics.

This Sudachi Edition delivers a flavor that is truly perfect for summer.

Personally, I recommend enjoying it chilled. The flavors of yuzu, sudachi, lemon, and lime are at their most balanced and enjoyable when served at refrigerator temperature.

Adding plenty of ice makes it even lighter and more refreshing by reducing the sweetness, but since the flavor is already quite delicate, too much chilling causes the rich citrus notes to fade. For the best experience, I think itâs best enjoyed at refrigerator temperature.

Contains 80mg of caffeine and 300mg of arginine.

The design combines a soft matte yellow as the main color with silver and a muted fawn tone, creating a three-color combination.

The matte texture and color palette give it the same premium feel that is characteristic of Red Bull designs. That said, the color is a little different from what I would normally associate with sudachi.

Sudachi is traditionally associated with a green color, but this flavor uses a unified yellow design worldwide. I assume the color was chosen to evoke more familiar citrus flavors such as yuzu, making the taste easier to imagine for people overseas who may not be familiar with sudachi.

This is the U.S. Summer Edition "Sudachi Lime," released as a seasonal summer flavor. Itâs exciting that Japan can now enjoy the latest global Red Bull flavor at the same time as other countries. The fact that a Japanese citrus fruit like sudachi was chosen is also something to appreciate as a Japanese consumer.

With its refreshing flavor thatâs perfect for summer, this is a release that makes me want to reach for another can.

name: Red Bull Total Zero Cherry Edition
description:
The Cherry Edition of the Red Bull Total Zero series, Wild Cherry. This is a zero-calorie, zero-sugar cherry-flavored drink. Along with the Orange Edition released at the same time, it disappeared from the shelves in less than a year as part of the Total Zero Editions.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

When opened, you can enjoy the sweet scent of cherry, light and refreshing. The typical cherry-flavored drinks usually have a rich, flavorful aroma that you can almost taste right away, but this Cherry Edition, being part of the Total Zero line, has a much more subdued fragrance.

When poured into a glass, the scent is much stronger than expected, and the cherry color is quite prominent. At first glance, you wouldn't think this is a zero-calorie, zero-sugar drinkâit looks like a regular, rich cherry-flavored energy drink.

As I take a sip... the balance between the light sweetness and the faint tartness of cherry is well-crafted. The aftertaste is very refreshing, with almost no lingering cherry flavor, which is typical of zero-calorie drinks. As a cherry flavor, itâs easy to understand, well-balanced, and excellent. However, if youâre expecting a bold, rich cherry taste, you may be disappointed.

The tartness isnât strong, making it easy to drink, but the sweetness has a noticeable artificial sweetener taste, which may be a dealbreaker for some. Itâs not the kind of sweetness that doesnât feel like a zero-calorie drink, like in the Monster Ultra or Rockstar Pure Zero series. Personally, I wouldâve liked the artificial sweetenerâs bitter-sweetness to be masked a bit more by the scent...

After drinking several cans, I realized that chilling it well reduces the artificial sweetener taste significantly, making it easier to drink. Additionally, drinking it straight from the can without using a glass enhances the carbonation, and the refreshing tartness of the cherry pairs well with the effervescence, making it delicious.

This Cherry Edition has a surprisingly good match with the light flavor, which made it quite enjoyable. The thinness typical of Total Zero drinks may be a little noticeable, but it never feels cheap or low-quality.

For those who like a refreshing, not-too-sweet cherry flavor or donât mind (or even enjoy) the aftertaste of artificial sweeteners, this would surely be a hitâa refreshing cherry-flavored drink. (Unfortunately, it was discontinued after about a year, which is a shame.)

It contains 114mg of caffeine, 1000mg of taurine, and artificial sweeteners like sucralose and acesulfame K, with citric acid and other ingredients to adjust the tartness.

There arenât any standout energy ingredientsâit's just the standard Red Bull blend.

The can design was great, and the flavor name, Wild Cherry, really piqued my excitement. However, when I tasted the ultra-light Zero Cherry flavor, I was kind of surprised in a way.

Itâs nothing like the regular Edition series; itâs the classic Total Zero taste. However, itâs not an overly artificial sweetener-heavy flavor either, so as a Zero Zero drink, itâs definitely well-executed.

If you prefer a light, refreshing fruit flavor, I definitely recommend the Total Zero Edition. But if youâre looking for a more intense and bold taste, Iâd suggest going for the regular Edition series.

This design is cool, but I do wish they had matched the tab design to the overall theme...

name: Red Bull Purple Edition Sugarfree
description:
The "world's first Purple Edition" was released as a sugar-free version in 2017 in the United States. Honestly, I didnât have high expectations when it was first released, but when I tried it, I was surprised by how well it turned out. I couldn't believe Red Bull could make such a great sugar-free drink!

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The strong blueberry-like aroma and vibrant purple color make it hard to believe this could be sugar-free. But how does it actually taste? Let's drink it and find out. Upon sipping, I'm amazed at the rich sweetness, reminiscent of grape, and it completely surprises me that this could be sugar-free. Typically, sugar-free Red Bull products have an overwhelming artificial sweetener taste, but this one is the opposite.

It beautifully masks the usual unpleasant aftertaste of artificial sweeteners, reaching a level of taste that almost feels like a regular sugary drink. The balance of sweetness and acidity from the berry flavor is excellent, and the aftertaste lingers with the berryâs taste and aromaâtruly impressive!

Especially for those who dislike the taste of artificial sweeteners, the aftertaste is significantly minimized, making this drink feel almost miraculous.

Interestingly, whether consumed at room temperature, chilled, or with ice, the sweetness level feels just like a sugared drink, making it a perfect refreshment.

Despite being discontinued in 2018, this drink is a perfect example of how a sugar-free product can exceed expectations. However, its sales performance was likely poor, and it might have been challenging for regular consumers, like me, to switch to sugar-free options after being used to sugary versions.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1320mg of taurine. While itâs sugar-free, it still has 15kcal, so itâs not a âtotal zeroâ product.

The purple can features the distinctive sugar-free design with light blue âSUGARFREEâ text, and a diagonal cut revealing the shiny silver underneathâthis became the signature design for Red Bullâs sugar-free edition series. When first released in 2017, the can did not have the blue "SUGARFREE" label at the top. This simple design was changed two months later, and the more recognizable sugar-free label was introduced. You can read more about it in our news article from that time.

After the product was discontinued in the U.S., the same purple edition was later released as full-sugar versions under the names Summer Edition, Purple Edition, and Acai Edition in Brazil and Europe.

Interestingly, the sugar-free version made a comeback in select European countries years after its initial discontinuation.

It's fascinating to see how energy drink brands evolve and how flavors can come back after time.

name: Red Bull Lime Edition Sugarfree
description:
The Sugarfree Lime Edition, released in the United States in 2017. Itâs more refined than expected, and the flavor is so good that you forget it's sugar-free. It was discontinued at the end of 2018.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. The liquid inside has a natural, light yellow-green color reminiscent of lime. I was a bit concerned by a somewhat artificial smell... Letâs take a sip. When I took a sip, the artificial vibe I noticed in the aroma completely disappeared, and I was surprised by how it tasted like a rich, sweetened limeade. This is delicious! I can't believe this is sugar-free limeade.

The balance between the rich sweetness of the limeade and the tangy acidity is great, and the unique aroma gives a nice lime peel feel. This is an unexpectedly tasty sugar-free limeade flavor. Most people probably wouldnât guess itâs sugar-free unless they were told.

For those who arenât fond of artificial sweeteners (like me), thereâs a slight aftertaste that reveals the distinct taste of artificial sweeteners, though itâs only noticeable at the very end. But I think this flavor and aroma would be widely accepted by most people.

In the end, it was discontinued after about a year, but something I noticed after drinking a few cans was that drinking 355ml at once felt too much, and the flavor became a bit monotonous after a while. If you sip it slowly, the flavor of the artificial sweeteners inevitably becomes noticeable. Itâs probably best enjoyed in the summer with ice, drinking it quickly.

Contains 114mg of caffeine and 1320mg of taurine. Itâs sugar-free, but with 15kcal of calories, itâs not a total zero product. Itâs part of the sugar-free series.

There were two designs for the Lime Edition Sugarfree. Initially released in 2017, the design on the left was the original. About two months later, a version with a light blue "SUGARFREE" label on the top of the can was released, which continued until it was discontinued. This made it much clearer that it was a sugar-free product. On the bottom right of the green can, thereâs a diagonal cut revealing a mirrored silver design, which became the design for the sugar-free versions of Red Bullâs Edition series released globally later on.

name: Red Bull Tropical Edition Sugarfree
description:
This is the Sugarfree version of the Tropical Edition released in the UK. The UK is one of the few countries where Sugarfree versions of the Edition series are often released.

Iâm excited to see how the zero-sugar version of this exquisite tropical fruit flavor has turned out.

In 2001, while living in the United States, I encountered energy drinks through the dance scene and was deeply impressed. After returning to Japan, I found that energy drinks were considered novelty beverages, so I established a comprehensive website in 2013 to share the true appeal of energy drinks. As an energy drink enthusiast, I began drinking them seriously again, collecting over 8,000 varieties of energy drinks from various countries. I am also active as a critic and expert, receiving media interviews.

The aroma is the same as the full-sugar Tropical Edition. You can't really feel the zero-sugar difference. It looks the same, and if youâre told itâs sugarfree, you might not even notice. When you drink it, the acidity is slightly subdued, and the richness is gone, replaced by a mellow sweetness like fruit candy. Knowing the deliciousness of the full-sugar version, this one feels a bit lacking in comparison.

Although the flavor of the artificial sweetener has been suppressed as much as possible, thereâs still a slight aftertaste that remains, and itâs a bit noticeable.
